If you’re fond of sloppy kisses, keen on chatty dogs, and are up for the challenge of training these two wannabe Alaskan Sled Dogs, then Fregs and Dickie might be for you!

name: Rae
description:
If you're looking for a little Rae of sunshine, you've just found her.

Sweet, affectionate, endlessly friendly and always ready for her next adventure, Rae is the kind of dog who makes every day feel a little bit brighter.

This clever girl has plenty of energy for adventures and loves getting out and about. When Rae isn't off enjoying her walks, she's at home showing off her second favourite hobby... digging! Rae is convinced every garden is hiding buried treasure, and she's appointed herself Chief Archaeologist to uncover it. Whether she's following an interesting scent or proudly admiring her latest excavation, she tackles every project with complete determination.

Her absolute best quality, though, is her love for people. Rae simply wants to be wherever you are. If she could magically shrink down and live in your pocket as your own little pocketful of sunshine, she absolutely would. She adores attention, thrives on affection and has never met a person she didn't want to be friends with. Whether you're relaxing on the sofa or pottering around the house, Rae will happily be your shadow, hoping there's a cuddle or ear scratch coming her way.

We're looking for an active home in a quieter area away from busy roads that can offer Rae plenty of adventures, enrichment and, ideally, a garden where the occasional dig spot won't cause too much heartbreak.

Adopt Rae today and we can almost guarantee a forecast of bright days, warm cuddles and a lifetime of sunshine.

name: Reenie
description:
Meet ‘teenie weenie’ Reenie

Reenie is a sweet and affectionate Greyhound looking for a patient home where she can enjoy life as a much-loved pet. As an ex-racer, she is still learning about home life and may need support settling into a routine, including house training and becoming accustomed to everyday household sights and sounds.

She enjoys her daily walks and loves the chance to have a run in a secure paddock before stretching out and relaxing on a comfy bed. Reenie will need access to a secure garden or regular access to a secure area for off-lead exercise. Due to her high prey drive, she must remain on lead when out and about and cannot live with cats or small animals.

Reenie can be around other dogs provided introductions are carried out carefully and at her pace. She generally prefers calm, low-key interactions and may be able to live with another Greyhound following successful introductions.

Reenie could live with primary school-aged children who understand the importance of giving her space when resting, as she can experience sleep startle and should always be left undisturbed while asleep.

This lovely girl is ready to leave her racing career behind and settle into a comfortable home where she can relax, build her confidence, and enjoy being part of the family.

name: Arlo
description:
Arlo is an affectionate and intelligent boy who is looking for an active home that can continue building on the great foundations he already has. Arlo can struggle to share his resources with people and other dogs, so we are looking for a home with secondary school aged children and no other pets in the home. He will need ongoing support with managing him around his food, and the team here can explain how to manage his environment and reinforce his recall to help him make good choices.

He loves people and is always keen to make new friends, often greeting visitors with lots of enthusiasm and a desire for attention. Arlo is keen to learn and already knows a range of cues and commands. He is highly motivated by food, toys and praise, and would love to learn new tricks and skills in his new home. He enjoys walks, and has excellent recall off lead. However, he will scavenge and try to pick up food while out and about, so ongoing training and management around this will be especially important, as he has a very sensitive tummy and needs a consistent diet.

If you are looking for an active, clever and fun companion who is eager to learn, Arlo could be a match for you - he will make a wonderful addition to the right home.

name: Angel
description:
Meet Angel, a characterful lady who loves to meet people, enjoy a good fuss and have a good time. She is happy to meet old and new friends alike; new owners will need to be aware of this because she is a stocky dog who could knock people over by accident.

Angel enjoys the simple pleasures in life but will need support with settling in to home life.

After a good walk, she enjoys lounging on the sofa, having some fuss, or basking in the sun.

Angel could live with older children, who are confident around larger dogs as she can be bouncy and a bit of a thug - typical of her breed! Angel enjoys saying hello to dogs here at the centre and will happily share walks with a new friend. She could live with a canine companion who enjoys bull breed style of play.

Things that are less familiar to Angel can sometimes be a little worrying for her causing Angel to bark so she might need some help in her new home.

Flat faced (brachycephalic) dogs suffer from additional health problems, which may impact their quality of life. We always recommend anyone thinking about adopting or buying a flat faced (brachycephalic) dog to thoroughly research the breed beforehand. Our expert team will be able to give you tips on exercise and weight management and advice on any support Angel may need.

if you have a sofa big enough for this cuddle-bug then please apply for her today.

name: Daisy
description:
Our Daisy has such a zest for life and loves to be out exploring, getting all the sniffs in on her walks and being part of the family.

Daisy is such a gentle girl who loves everyone she meets. She does sometimes get excitable when meeting new humans so we are teaching her that all the love comes when she has 4 paws on the floor.

Daisy has lived with children before and could do so again in her new home.

She could potentially live with a well matched dog, that has lived with dogs before, pending meets at the centre.

Due to Daisy having a high prey drive, she wouldn't be able to live with cats or small animals.

If you think you could offer Daisy a comfy spot on the sofa and a place in your heart, then we look forward to hearing from you.

name: Shaxx
description:
Meet the stunning Shaxx!

Shaxx is a full of life, young German Shepard. He is a gorgeous boy with lots of love to give. Shaxx is looking for a home where his new owners can be home for some of the day to keep him company. He will also be looking for owners who can continue his basic training needs.

Pending on successful meets here at the centre, Shaxx has the potential to live with another dog. The resident dog would need to of lived with a dog before, or be used to a large bouncy dog.  He wouldn't be able to live with other pets.

Shaxx could live with older teenage children in his new home, that are used to large dogs.

Shaxx is strong on lead and will need owners who are physically able to handle him, to be able to meet his exercise needs. Knowledge of the German Shepard breed is desirable but not a must.

if you think you could offer our Super Shaxx a new home, then we look forward to hearing from you.

name: Earl
description:
These sweet boys are looking for a very quiet, patient home willing to give them the time they need to thrive in the real world. They’ve had very little exposure to life and need time to learn what a family can be. They need a home where everyone is a teen upwards and ideally with no other pets.

This gorgeous pair don’t seem to have had the best start to life and now need that chance to see how great life can be. They’re a bonded pair and gain confidence and reassurance from each other so really would prefer to be rehomed together (double collie cuteness!!). Currently they aren’t ready to go for walks but would love a family able to support them to reach their full potential in time.

name: August
description:
These sweet boys are looking for a very quiet, patient home willing to give them the time they need to thrive in the real world. They’ve had very little exposure to life and need time to learn what a family can be. They need a home where everyone is a teen upwards and ideally with no other pets.

This gorgeous pair don’t seem to have had the best start to life and now need that chance to see how great life can be. They’re a bonded pair and gain confidence and reassurance from each other so really would prefer to be rehomed together (double collie cuteness!!). Currently they aren’t ready to go for walks but would love a family able to support them to reach their full potential in time.

name: Milo
description:
Milo would be best suited to a home where any children are sensible and of upper secondary ages, being mindful of his nervous nature. Milo would like to be the only pet in the home as he has shown to chase smaller animals. He would enjoy a family that can continue to work on his confidence around other dogs out and about. Milo would benefit from a secure garden but homes without a garden may be considered in quiet areas. As he can be worried by new experiences and busy environments, we advise he is kept on his lead and separated from the front door as he can be a flight risk when fearful. Milo can be worried for his vet visits and may need to be muzzled for this, so a home happy to work on his confidence would be great for him.

Milo is our sweet and sensitive 5 year old Dachshund looking for a calm home to settle his paws into. Milo has found kennel life a little overwhelming so will likely take sometime to feel confident in his forever home. This lovely boy has shown to enjoy the company of smaller dogs, following them on his walks and he has previously been playful with squeaky toys. He would love a quiet, patient home that can take things at his pace so that he has the space to feel secure enough to let his personality shine.

name: Delilah
description:
Delilah is a friendly and affectionate Boxer who absolutely loves being around people. She's the kind of dog who will happily seek out fuss and cuddles, leaning into her favourite humans for extra attention. Since arriving in foster care, she's shown just how much she enjoys company and being part of family life.
While Delilah has lots of love to give, she's still adjusting to a world that feels quite new to her. New environments, loud noises and car travel can make her feel unsure, so she's looking for patient adopters who can help build her confidence at her own pace. Delilah would like to be the only dog in her new home and would benefit from a private garden where she can continue to feel safe and secure while settling in. She could live with older children who can enjoy her affectionate, sometimes bouncy nature.

If you're looking for a loving companion who thrives on human company, Delilah could be the perfect match. She enjoys meeting new people, loves a cuddle, and is always happy to stay close to those she trusts. Her foster carers have seen her become more settled each day, and she's already showing what a wonderful addition she could be to a family.
Delilah is still learning that the world isn't such a scary place, so she'll need adopters who can continue supporting her with confidence-building, especially around car travel and unfamiliar situations. In return, you'll gain a loyal, affectionate best friend who will be delighted to share plenty of cuddles, companionship and classic Boxer enthusiasm with her new family.

name: Shiva
description:
Shiva is a 2 month old German Shepherd X Belgian Shepherd Pup. He is looking for a fairly active home that can help him learn all the basics to thrive in life. He has the potential to live with another dog pending meets at the centre and could live with other animals providing initial introductions are carefully managed. He could live with children of Primary School age and older that are confident around dogs as he can show typical puppy behaviour such as jumping up and mouthing. He will need his own, secure garden to provide space for training, exercise and play until he is fully vaccinated and can explore the wider world

Shiva is a friendly pup who loves to play with teddies and likes a lap to cuddle up into. He will make a lovely addition to his new home.

name: Patch
description:
Patch will benefit from adopters who feel confident supporting a dog who is reactive around other dogs due to frustration. He has, on occasion, redirected this frustration, so he’ll be wearing a muzzle and staying on lead during walks. Due to this, Patch would love a home with access to quiet walks away from lots of dogs. He is looking for a  private, secure garden to have a peaceful space to relax and play, it would not be ideal for Patch to have neighbouring dogs as this would increase his frustration levels in the home. Patch is happiest as the only pet in the home and can live with secondary‑school‑aged children but would need to be adults only to walk.

Patch is a lovely, friendly and excitable two‑year‑old Foxhound who has had an unsettled start in life, yet still greets the world with enthusiasm and a huge heart. He adores toys, playtime and anything that lets him burn off energy, and he throws himself joyfully into every game. Adventures are one of his favourite things — he happily jumps straight into the car, eager to see what the day holds. Patch is incredibly affectionate, loves being close to his people, and enjoys feeling part of whatever’s going on. He’s also very food‑motivated, which makes training fun and rewarding, and he thrives when given chances to learn, play and connect.

name: Thornton
description:
Thornton is a 2 month old German Shepherd X Belgian Shepherd Pup. He is looking for a fairly active home that can help him learn all the basics to thrive in life. He has the potential to live with another dog pending meets at the centre and could live with other animals providing initial introductions are carefully managed. He could live with children of Primary School age and older that are confident around dogs as he can show typical puppy behaviour such as jumping up and mouthing. He will need his own, secure garden to provide space for training, exercise and play until he is fully vaccinated and can explore the wider world.

Thornton is a friendly pup who loves to play with toys and is already showing an interest in training - especially if a tasty treat or two are involved. He will make a lovely addition to his new home.

name: Wanda
description:
Meet Wanda a beautiful 2 month old German Shepherd cross Belgium Shepherd on the look out for her forever home. She can live with other dogs as long as fully vaccinated and any dog of the opposite sex is neutered, pending successful meets at the centre. Wanda can live with older primary school children who are used to dogs that may jump up or have the occassional puppy mouthing.

As Wanda is a puppy she will need to have any leaving hours gradually introduced and must have a secure garden due to not being fully vaccinated. 
Do you have room in your hearts and homes for this delightful girl who is on the look out for her new adventure.

name: Sizzles
description:
Sizzles is an older gentleman who is used to his home comforts. He’s an adorable chap who can live with children of primary school age. Sizzles can be vocal when he sees other dogs but is able to share walks with some calmer pooches. He does ask to be the only pet in the home though.

Sizzles is an 11 year old Border Terrier who came into our care as his owners were moving abroad. He’s got a really good home history and so it shouldn’t take him long to settle back in to home life. He’s fully housetrained, good in the car, and happy being left home alone for a few hours too. Sizzles loves spending time with people and will often be found asking for fuss.

name: Cooper
description:
Cooper is a 7 year old Husky x Pomeranian. He is looking for a home where he can be the only pet as while he is happy to have doggy friends on walks he is not fond of sharing his toys. Cooper can be worried by younger children, he may have the potential to join a home with a child of Older Seconday School age (14+) pending meets at the centre. Cooper is toilet trained and would like access to his own secure garden to help him settle into his new home. Though he has previously been left longer hours, he has had a lot of change in his life recently and has started showing some seperation anxiety so would like someone at home with him most of the time initially and any leaving hours will need to be built up slowly once he has settled into his new home and routine.

Cooper is a friendly boy who loves spending time with people. He enjoys a fuss and loves playing with toys. Cooper loves going on walks and finding lots of interesting sniffs. He walks nicely on lead but can pull if there is something he wants to investigate so will need adopters who can manage this. He has a prey drive and will need to be kept on lead when outside of the home. Can you offer this delightful chap a forever home?

name: Gertrude
description:
Say hi to Gertrude, a 10 month old Cane Corso cross! A sweet, affectionate girl, Gerty has a joyful zest for life that is absolutely infectious. She can be a little reserved when meeting new people, but once she warms up to you, she’s your friend for life. You’ll be rewarded with plenty of attention and affection as Gerty loves nothing more than leaning in for cuddles and trying to sit on your lap. She enjoys playing with soft toys and balls and occasionally likes a good game of fetch. This playful, lovely girl would love a home with all the love and time to give her to thrive.

Gertrude is looking for a home where she can have her own garden, as she absolutely loves playing and having zoomies, but she’s also a bit of an anxious girl around new people so this will be beneficial for introductions. As she can be a bit worried around traffic, she would be best suited to a home in a smaller residential area. Due to her bouncy nature, she could live with upper secondary school aged children who can respect her boundaries, and she’d prefer to be the only pet in the home but would enjoy having doggy friends to go out on walks with. As she’s a clever girl, she would benefit from training and learning a few more manners.

name: Rose
description:
Beautiful Rose is a 11 month old Staffie looking for an active and loving home. Rose is a very affectionate and loving young dog who enjoys being close to her people and loves nothing more than cuddling up with her favourite people. She enjoys a fuss and will often come looking for a stroke if you stop giving her attention! She is friendly and enjoys meeting both people and other dogs, and she has a fun, playful side too, particularly when there’s a soft toy around for a game of tuggy. With her young age and energy, Rose will keep you busy and would love to have an owner who enjoys getting out and about exploring and savouring adventures together.

Rose would suit a home on the outskirts of a city or in a smaller town, as she’s an easy-going girl and not phased around traffic and people. She is happy walking alongside busier roads but she would also enjoy getting in the car and heading off to quieter places for lovely sniffy walks. Rose would benefit from having some doggy friends to walk with and could live with dog savvy secondary school aged children. She is friendly with new people and is happy to have regular visitors in the home. Rose can find being left alone difficult, so she will need someone who can keep leaving to a minimum to begin with and is willing to gradually build this up with her.

name: Cashew
description:
Cashew is a lively boy who loves nothing more than bounding about. He likes to use his voice but is friendly and can live with children of secondary school age. Cashew can share his walks with dogs as long as they are happy with him talking to them on approach. He will need to be the only dog in the home though. He has potential to live with cats, pending a successful scent swap and gradual introductions.

Cashew is only 2 years old and came into us with no home history. He might appreciate an introduction to the basics such as car travel and housetraining. No introductions are needed for zooming though, as he will bounce around a paddock to his heart’s content before coming over to his people for some light fuss.

name: Pippin
description:
Meet Pippin, our super cool and full of fun Frenchie Cross. He's on the search for a forever home with adopters who can help build his confidence and help him blossom. Pippin can find meeting new people a little scary, but with some patience (and a few toys) he soon comes around to show you what a fun loving boy he really is! Pippin could live with college aged children following a meeting here at the centre.. Pippin would love a home where he can enjoy quieter walkies away from heavy traffic and busy roads, as he can find this quite scary. He is a social boy and enjoys making doggy friends, so he could share his new home with another dog following a meeting at the centre. As Pippin LOVES his toys, any toy time will need to be carefully supervised.

Pippin is a super little guy who loves nothing more than play time. He can sometimes be less confident that he seems, so his new family will need to be committed to understanding how he may be feeling and learning to read his body language. Pippin can find being left for long periods a little stressful so would like adopters who can build any time being left gradually as he settles into his forever home. He is such a fun little dude who will bring so much joy to his forever family!

name: Andres
description:
Meet Andres, a big, lovable 9 year old male crossbreed boy weighing around 45 kg, who’s ready to find his perfect match.

Andres absolutely adores people — and if you’re a woman, you might just become his favourite human instantly. He’s a friendly, easy going companion who fits beautifully into daily life.

Great with dogs and gentle with kidsHouse-trained and clean indoorsTravels well in the carWalks like a dream on the leashLoves water and bath timeCan stay home alone calmly (may bark if he hears unusual noises outside)Confident and relaxed in busy city environments — crowds and traffic don’t bother him at allPlease note: Andres cannot live with cats or small animals.

We’re looking for an experienced large-dog owner — ideally a woman — who can offer:

A home with a gardenAnother calm, confident dog companionUnderstanding of big dog needs and behaviour

Currently located outside of the UK, Andres is a wonderful, balanced dog who will bring loyalty, companionship, and a lot of love into the right home.

name: Trico
description:
Trico is a 4 year old male Gascon Saintongeois Cross.

After a really long wait at the pound, TRICO was recently released and he is proving to be the sweetest soul!

Currently in a foster home, his carer says he is a timid chap with people, but friendly with other dogs and super clean indoors.

Trico never gets into trouble! TRICO passions, so far, are food and he loves a scent too.

TRICO is such a lovely little man who needs a family of his own, a patient owner who can help him blossom.

TRICO he is castrated, vaccinated, microchipped, blood tested, he has a passport and he can pack his bags if the right family appears.

He is currently in Spain but can travel abroad, the charity arranges all the paperwork and transport.

name: Milo
description:
Milo is a 5 year old male Spanish Hound Cross.

Milo is such a good boy, friendly, calm and clean.

Even cats are no issue for him! Milo would really like to have a loving home at last, someone who sees what a wonderful boy he is.

Milo is castrated, vaccinated, microchipped, blood tested, he has a passport and he can pack his bags if the right family appears.

He is currently in Spain but can travel abroad, the charity arranges all the paperwork and transport.

name: Daisy
description:
Daisy is a six month old female cross breed puppy who currently weighs around twelve kilograms and is expected to reach approximately twenty kilograms when fully grown.

She is fostered in a home in Bulgaria, where she has settled beautifully and is ready to travel to the United Kingdom once the right family is found.

Daisy is fully vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, clinically healthy, and will travel with an EU pet passport and all required documentation.

Daisy is an exceptionally calm, gentle, and easy-going puppy. Despite her young age, she has wonderful house manners and has adapted brilliantly to life in a home.

She is clean indoors, settles well, and happily stays home alone for a few hours without causing any damage or becoming distressed.

name: Sadie
description:
SADIE – FOUR YEARS OF LOVE, STILL WAITING FOR HER PERSON

Four years. That’s how long Sadie has been waiting. Four years of wagging her tail for every visitor, hoping today might be her day.

Four years of pressing her head into the hands of rescuers, desperate to be someone’s dog. Four years of watching others leave while she stayed behind.

Sadie is love in its purest form. She is human-oriented in every way, craving touch, affection, and closeness. She is cuddly beyond words, the kind of dog who melts into your arms.

She is loyal and devoted, ready to give her whole heart to the person who finally chooses her. But Sadie has never been chosen. She doesn’t understand why.

She doesn’t know that dogs like her—dogs who don’t like sharing their humans—often wait the longest. Because Sadie isn’t just loyal—she is fiercely devoted.

She doesn’t just want love—she wants to protect it. She doesn’t want to share her human—she wants to belong to them, and only them.

Sadie is not a dog for just any home. She is a dog for someone who wants an unbreakable bond. Someone who will be her world, just as she will be theirs.

At 6 years old, Sadie is still waiting. She is not meant to be one of many. She is meant to be someone’s one and only. Sadie needs to be the only dog in the home.

She will love her person beyond measure—and fiercely protect them from every other dog. She is waiting for the human who needs her as much as she needs them. Could that person be you?

6 years old (March 2025) – four years of waiting for her chanceMiddle-sized, stunning, and full of loveDeeply affectionate, cuddly, and human-orientedLoyal beyond words—ready to give her whole heartNeeds to be the only dog in the homeWill protect her human from every other dog

Fully VaccinatedSpayed4D TestedBrucellosis TestedMicrochippedFull RBU

Sadie has waited long enough. Could you be the one to finally take her home? Please get in touch today!

name: Max
description:
A strikingly handsome, loyal, intelligent boy who is ready for his new life.

Max is the kind of dog who makes an impression the moment you meet him — confident, affectionate, and beautifully connected to his people. At 30 kg, he’s a solid lad with a gentle heart and a playful spirit.

Great with other dogs — social, friendly, easy-going

Very loyal and smart — bonds deeply, learns quickly

Loves being brushed, fussed, and played with

Excellent at the vets, calm and cooperative

Plays happily with our 14?year?old work experience student

Has interacted with small dogs and younger children with no issues

Car rides aren’t his favourite yet — most likely because he was abandoned and fears it may happen again. But he’s improving every week, learning that car trips now mean safety, not abandonment.

And truly… he has the best set of pearly white teeth we’ve ever seen.

Max is an all?around super boy who will thrive with:

An active family, Someone home often, Children 10+ due to his size – A home that values companionship, routine, and fun

Max is fully vaccinated, neutered, and ready to fly on August 2nd. For everyone’s comfort and safety, children in the household must be 10+ due to his size.

name: Newton
description:
Newton, approximately 4 yrs old, large, crossbreed.

Newton can only be described as a cuddly bear! He loves people, adores attention, and thinks he’s still a pup. Despite his size he will try to climb on your lap for cuddles.

Newton is a stunning boy with the softest coat and the most loving nature. He’s incredibly cuddly, adores human interaction, and will happily lean in for a good neck scratch and cuddle any chance he gets.

His affectionate personality makes him a truly special companion and it is a testament to him, given the situation he has found himself in.

Newton has been with shelter for a while and, sadly, no one ever came forward to claim him. Given his loving and gentle nature, we think he had a home before and had humans that he loved, even if this wasn’t reciprocated.

Despite this, he remains full of love and is quite happy-go-lucky.

He is a strong boy, so he will thrive in a home with experienced owners. He walks nicely on the leash. Newton gets along well with female dogs of a similar size but can’t live with males or smaller dogs.

He’s not just looking for a home—he’s looking for someone who understands him, can guide him, and will give him the love and structure he needs to truly flourish.

In return, you’ll gain a loyal, affectionate companion who will be by your side through everything. He would suit an active family (children 10+ due to size), single person, or a couple.

Newton can be adopted in the UK or Cyprus. His adoption fees are sponsored so, if travelling to the UK, we are just asking for travel costs to be covered.

He is ready to fly. He is vaccinated, castrated, and has had a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Roy
description:
Roy is a 1.5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is an amazing, happy and friendly boy who is looking for his forever home. With his cheerful personality and beautiful smile, Roy is hoping to find a family who will love him for the rest of his life.

Roy is very friendly with people and enjoys spending time with them. He also gets on well with other dogs and is suitable to live in a home with canine companions. His happy nature makes him a wonderful companion.

Roy has not yet been tested with cats, so it is not known whether he could live with them. He is suitable to live with older children, making him a good match for families with sensible older youngsters.

He is looking for a home where he can continue to be happy and loved.

Roy is currently based in Cyprus but can travel to the UK or elsewhere in Europe once he has been adopted. He is ready to make the journey to his forever family when the right home comes along.

He is waiting for someone to give him the chance he deserves.

Roy will be adopted with a full adoption package. This includes vaccinations, a microchip, blood tests and neutering before he joins his new home. Rescue backup and support will be provided, and a home check applies as part of the adoption process.

name: Hermes
description:
Hermes is a 1.5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a sweet, gentle and friendly young dog who is looking for his forever home. He gets along beautifully with everyone he meets and has a lovely nature.

Hermes enjoys being around people and makes a wonderful companion. His friendly personality means he is happy to spend time with those around him. He is also social with other dogs and is suitable to live with them.

Hermes has not yet been tested with cats, so it is not known whether he could live with them. He is suitable to live with older children, making him a good match for families with sensible older youngsters.

He is looking for a loving home where he can continue to thrive.

Hermes is currently based in Cyprus but is able to travel to the UK or anywhere in Europe once he has been adopted. He is ready to make the journey to begin a new life with his forever family.

He is hoping to find a home where he will be loved and cared for.

Hermes will be rehomed with a full adoption package. His vaccinations are up to date, and he is microchipped, blood tested and neutered.

Full rescue backup will be provided, and a home check is required before his adoption can be completed.

name: Mura
description:
MURA is a medium size loving German Shepherd crossbreed girl of 5 years who has sadly had to grow up in the shelter in Spain since she was a puppy.

She adores people and is slowly growing in confidence as she is finally getting out to explore the world. She is well behaved on the lead and is quickly adapting to new situations but needs more life experience.

We are confident Mura will make a fantastic family dog given time. She is intelligent, obedient, eager to please and quick to learn and kennel clean.

Mura’s brother was adopted a couple of years ago in the UK and has grown into the perfect dog and companion. Mura would be okay to live with dog savvy children 12 years and over and is suitable to train to live with a cat if required.

She is neutered, inoculated, microchipped, etc with no known health issues and is available for meet and greets from our premises in Wistaston, Cheshire by appointment only.

name: Bianca
description:
Bianca is a 3-year-old female Husky-Cross. This medium-large girl, weighing approximately 25kg, has already been through more than most dogs should ever have to.

Found starving and alone on the streets of Cyprus, she was so desperate for food that she was eating scraps alongside a colony of cats.

Emaciated, weak, and suffering from leishmania, she had clearly been abandoned once her illness made her “inconvenient.”

But despite the pain and neglect she endured, Bianca never gave up. She quietly accepted her rescue, knowing on some deep level that things were about to change.

Thanks to an incredible foster family, Bianca has transformed. With love, vet care, and proper medication, she has overcome her leishmania — now fully recovered and thriving.

She just needs a simple tablet twice a day to keep the condition in check. It’s manageable, doesn’t increase insurance premiums or affect her quality of life, and is absolutely worth it for a dog who gives love as fiercely as Bianca does.

For the past1 year, Bianca has been living in a foster home and learning how to be a dog again. She’s fully house trained, understands basic commands, and walks well on the leash.

She’s food motivated, making her very trainable — and she’s totally obsessed with squeaky balls. Her ideal day? A long sniffy walk, a fun play session, and cuddles with her favourite humans.

Bianca is incredibly affectionate and loyal to her circle, though she can take a little time to warm up to strangers. Once you’re in her heart though, you’re there for life.

She’s not keen on other animals and must be the only pet in the home. That said, she’s all the dog you’ll ever need — her love runs deep.

Her perfect match would be someone who loves big, bold personalities with even bigger hearts. An active home is ideal, with people who appreciate her breed’s intelligence and energy.

While experience with dogs — especially Huskies — is helpful, it’s not a strict requirement. What matters most is a loving, understanding home that’s ready to give this beautiful girl the second chance she’s waited so long for.

Bianca can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. She has been tested for other infectious diseases, is spayed, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Dante
description:
Dante is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-sized dog who is described as handsome, loving and affectionate. Dante is also obedient and quick to learn, making him a wonderful companion for a family looking for a friendly and sensible dog.

He is very good on the lead and has no known fears. Dante is sociable with all dogs and enjoys being around other canine companions.

His happy nature and confident personality help him settle well into different situations.

Dante is kennel clean and has no health issues reported. He is a cheerful and well-balanced dog who appears to take life in his stride.

His affectionate temperament means he enjoys spending time with people and forming strong bonds with those around him.

He could live with other dogs in his new home and would be suitable for families with dog-savvy children aged 12 years and over. Consideration may also be given to families with younger children.

His loving and sensible nature suggests he would enjoy being part of an active and caring household.

Dante has been neutered, inoculated and microchipped. He is available for meet and greets by appointment from the rescue premises in Wistaston, Cheshire. He is a happy, affectionate and sociable dog who is ready to find a loving forever home.

name: Frida
description:
Frida is a medium size very pretty crossbreed girl of just 4 years.

She is very loving, intelligent, affectionate and obedient, a real people dog. She can live alongside other dogs but would be happier I think as an only dog.

She is very well behaved on the lead, not reactive and is confident, well behaved and responsive on her walks. Frida is kennel clean and would make a great family friend for adventures and fun.

Frida would be okay to live with dog savvy children 12 years and over. Would consider families with younger children too.

She is neutered, inoculated, microchipped, etc and is available for meet and greets from our premises in Wistaston, Cheshire by appointment only.

name: Kayan
description:
Kayan is a very handsome boy of 7 years young who is a large size Mastin cross.

He is very loving and affectionate dog, a real gentle soul in a large body. He is very good with other dogs and would be suitable to live with dog savvy children 12 years and older.

Kayan is a very happy dog who is very obedient and quick to learn. He is kennel clean and well behaved on the lead and is not reactive.

He loves his walks and is desperate for a family of his own, he has waited a long time.

He is neutered, inoculated, microchipped, etc and is available for meet and greets from our premises in Wistaston, Cheshire by appointment only.

name: Danny
description:
Danny is a beautiful and handsome, young Collie/Pointer cross Mastin boy, with a short, black and white flecked coat. Poor boy has had a terrible experience of life so far, but now things are turning around for him.

Danny is very sweet natured, with a big heart and lots of trust and affection to humans being kind to him.

Danny started life scavenging for scraps, terrified of people. A kind volunteer began leaving out food for him and he would eat it and even play with her dogs, but he would bolt the second she got close.

When a cruel neighbour started throwing stones at him and threatening his life, she knew she had to save him from that place and move him urgently.

When he arrived in foster care, Danny was a different kind of broken — frozen with fear, hiding in corners, too scared even to be moved. But with his foster housemates by his side, Danny slowly started to come back to life.

Fast forward a few weeks, and this boy is unrecognisable. He is now playful, affectionate, cheerful, and SO ready to give and receive love.

He’s still a little shy in new places and with loud noises which is understandable but he’s intelligent, eager to learn, and already walking beautifully on the lead, trotting alongside a bike, and settling nicely in the car.

Danny loves his doggy friends but has not yet been tested with cats.

Danny didn’t have an easy start, but he never stopped trusting that good things were possible. Now he just needs someone to give him the home he’s been waiting for. And needs someone with time and patience to let him blossom.

Danny is neutered, up to date with vaccinations and had clear blood tests, and tested negative for Brucella

We are looking for a family with another friendly dog for Danny to play with and learn from, and older calm children no younger than 11yrs to suit his level of confidence.

Good on lead, good with bikes, good in the car Good other dogs and people. Smart, affectionate, and blossoming every day.

name: Orion
description:
Orion is a 1 year old, medium-large, male, Cross-Breed, who is a sweet, friendly, lovely boy waiting for his forever home. He has never truly known what it means to be a carefree puppy.

He should be enjoying life in a loving home, cared for and cherished, warm at night instead of sleeping on a concrete floor.

Confiscated from his owners, Orion and his three siblings have all been in the shelter since they were just young pups. Arguably, it was the best thing to happen to them, but now they each really need a home and family to call their own.

Orion is a medium-large dog who will need ongoing training to help him settle into home life. He has gotten used to walking on a lead and is well behaved on walks.

He is also wonderful with other dogs and children. Even though he is young, Orion and all of his siblings give off a lovely calming energy and we suspect they will be medium energy once in a home.

Orion is far too young to spend his days in a shelter and has missed an important stage of learning and exploring, but it’s never too late for dogs! He could live with a single person, a couple, or a family. A secure garden and nice walks would be ideal.

Orion can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. He will be tested for infectious diseases, is castrated, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

Please help give this lovely boy the life he deserves.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Willow
description:
Willow is a 1 year old, medium-sized, female Cross-Breed who is a friendly, happy girl eagerly waiting for her forever home. She does not know what being a puppy truly means.

She should be enjoying life in a loving home, cared for and cherished, warm at night instead of sleeping on a concrete floor.

Confiscated from her owners, Willow and her three siblings have all been in the shelter since they were just young pups. Arguably, it was the best thing to happen to them, but now they each really need a home and family to call their own.

Willow is a medium-sized dog who will need ongoing training to help her settle into home life. She has gotten used to walking on a lead and is well behaved on walks. She is also wonderful with other dogs and children.

Even though she is young, Willow and all of her siblings give off a lovely calming energy and we suspect they will be medium energy once in a home.

Willow is far too young to spend her days in a shelter and has missed an important stage of learning and exploring, but it’s never too late for dogs! She could live with a single person, a couple, or a family. A secure garden and nice walks would be ideal.

Willow can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. She has been tested for infectious diseases, is spayed, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Casper
description:
Meet Casper, a 5 year old male Cross-Breed who’s been waiting far too long for his shot at happiness. He’s currently based at Simba Shelter in Cyprus and has sadly become one of their longest residents.

Well over a year he has been in the shelter and you can actually see the sadness in his eyes.

How can a dog that looks like Casper have been in the shelter for all this time. Is it his age? The fact that he’s not small and fluffy? He deserves a second chance in life just as much as the desirable-looking dogs.

And the most heartbreaking thing is his affinity for humans. He doesn’t get out of his kennel much but, when he does, he relishes at the opportunity for some human affection.

In his current situation, he shows less interest in his actual walks and more interest in humans.

Casper is a profoundly wonderful dog on so many levels. Not only is he incredibly handsome, but he’s also clever and eager to please. He would suit an adopter willing to take the time to get to know him, train him, and invest in his potential.

Casper has shared his space with female dogs but has shown to be generally quite selective with canines. As a result, he requires a pet/dog-free home.

As with any rescue dog, Casper needs time and structure to settle into home life. In return, Casper will give back tenfold — loyalty, love, and gratitude in abundance.

Having known hardship and the loss of a family (we think he had a home before), Casper will be one of those eternally grateful dogs.

They are simply a joy to take under your wing and watch thrive in a home. And we, as volunteers, love to see this. It is exactly why we volunteer in dog rescue, to see dogs like Casper come out the other side and get their happy ending.

We provide full rescue back up and provide guidance and support throughout a dogs life.

Casper’s adoption fee is sponsored due to the length of time he has been in the shelter.

Casper is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and be tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and castrated.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Lykos
description:
Lykos is a 7-8 year old mixed breed who sadly came into the shelter after his elderly owner passed away and none of his family members were able to take his dog in.

It’s always particularly sad to see dogs that are accustomed to living in a home try and adjust to the shelter, as it’s so overwhelming, confusing and scary for them.

Despite his slightly older age, Lykos has slowly but surely adapted well, and now he’s ready to find a forever home for his later years.

Lykos is around eight years old and is a sweet, calm boy with a gentle nature. Right now he’s sharing his kennel with a female dog who he enjoys hanging out with.

He was previously in a kennel on his own, so we think he’s quite liked having a friend come to join him.

Although he’s a little older than most of our other shelter residents, Lykos still really likes going out for walks and is well mannered on the lead.

He loves sniffing through the long grass, peeing on anything that’s already been peed on, and he also likes to just stand and observe, taking in his surroundings.

He enjoys basking in the sun on a warm day, and he’s also quite a nosey neighbour so he loves watching what everyone else is up to.

Lykos finds the close capacity of the kennels quite confronting, and he really doesn’t like being barked at by other dogs in surrounding kennels.

He would definitely prefer a calm household with a laidback lifestyle, and we don’t think he would be too fussed either way if he was the only dog, or if he shared with a resident dog.

He can be quite independent, but if he was homed with another dog we think he’d be happiest with a female simply based on his experience in the shelter.

Being an older dog, Lykos is looking for a patient family. Just because he’s been in a home before, it doesn’t mean he will adapt seamlessly, and he still requires understanding and time to settle in properly.

A UK companion home is still very different to a Cyprus companion home, and there will be a lot of change for him to navigate.

The perfect home for Lykos would be based in a calm, residential area, or semi-rurally, with direct access to a secure garden. He would suit an older family given his calmer nature, or a younger family just wanting to give a senior dog a happy life.

He’d enjoy leisurely walks in the woods or along the beach, but he won’t be too demanding in his exercise needs. As long as he has a comfortable bed and lots of attention, we think he’ll be very happy.

name: Aspen
description:
Aspen is a 10 month old Beagle mix who’s life got off to a very rocky start. He was abandoned as a young puppy in Cyprus and found seriously unwell with parvovirus.

After spending time in the vets and making a full recovery, he joined the shelter and eventually travelled to the UK as a foster.

Since arriving, it’s been a bit of a journey for him, and it’s taken time to really understand what he needs to feel settled and secure.

After struggling to find the right fit in a home environment, Aspen has spent the last couple of months in kennels, where he has surprised everyone with just how well he’s done.

With clear routines, patient handling and consistent care, he has really come into himself. He’s responded brilliantly to basic training, built very strong relationships with the staff and grown hugely in confidence.

Aspen is a clever, energetic young dog, but new and unfamiliar situations can still feel overwhelming for him, and are often made more challenging by the fact that he is deaf.

Aspen is great with people and has been incredibly sociable, affectionate and engaged with those caring for him. Everyone who has been involved with him at the kennels has been really charmed by his personality.

He’s a cheeky, busy puppy who loves cuddles, fuss and being the centre of attention. Once he feels safe, his personality really shines and he shows just how much he enjoys human company.

When it comes to other dogs, Aspen is more selective. While he has previously lived alongside other dogs, is kennelled parallel to other dogs, and can pass dogs calmly on walks, we think that overall he would be happiest as the only dog in the home.

We suspect that earlier experiences may have left him feeling automatically defensive, and giving him a space where he doesn’t have to share attention or resources will help him relax and feel secure.

We are looking for an adult only home without other pets. As Aspen is deaf, it’s important that his environment is predictable and calm, and we don’t feel it would be fair to place him in a home with children or cats.

He would thrive in a quieter, more rural setting with access to a garden and plenty of opportunity to burn off energy in a safe way.

Aspen is clever and has learned hand signals for certain commands, so he would love to continue with further training as he really likes to learn and engage.

Aspen needs a confident, committed adopter who understands that he’s a young dog who has had a lot of upheaval in a short space of time.

With the right people, he lights up and shows what a sweet, silly and loving boy he really is.

Experience with training or deaf dogs would be helpful but isn’t essential, as long as his new family are patient, open to learning and ready to give him the structure and stability he’s been missing.

name: Prince
description:
Prince is a 20 month old Lurcher and he is looking for a new home. Although he’s not originally an Underdog, when we heard that he needed some support we wanted to try and help him.

Unfortunately, Prince is living in a home that is not suitable for his needs. He has been struggling in the city and needs a less overwhelming environment to call home.

He is also a very energetic boy, and is looking for an active, patient and understanding family.

Prince is just under two years old and is a sighthound mix. He was part of an accidental litter, and was bought as a puppy, but has consistently struggled in London and requires a more experienced handler.

With the support of a local day-care and dog walking business, Prince has had a lot more exposure to other dogs and new people, and he has made a lot of progress regarding his confidence and social skills.

We think this will continue to improve in a semi-rural area.

Prince is adorable and has a very loving, affectionate nature with those he knows. He loves to give cuddles and is really friendly once he has formed a bond with you.

He is however apprehensive of strangers, and needs time to get used to new people. Although Prince doesn’t like being in big groups of dogs in day-care setting, he is very happy on group walks and trots along happily with them.

Prince has been handled quite roughly in the past which has left him sensitive to touch. He has been muzzle trained to make vet visits more manageable, and he also wears this when on walks in case he meets a dog he feels uncomfortable around.

During the day, Prince is quite happy to be left alone for a few hours. He is housetrained and enjoys playing with toys. He has been conditioned to race after a ball when out on walks, so this is his primary source of exercise and he is very ball driven.

He has responded well to training and is generally a very good boy who is eager to please. He sits and waits for his food and takes treats nicely, but doesn’t like to be approached whilst he is eating.

Prince loves spending time in the countryside where he has more space to run around. He would love a home with a big garden and an active lifestyle, and he’s much calmer outside of the hustle and bustle of London.

We would love to see him get the second chance that he deserves in a more suitable home where he can get the attention, focus and training that he thrives on.

name: Jessie
description:
Jessie is a four month old female Labrador cross. Her litter arrived in the shelter when they were just one month old, after their mum was found as a stray.

Unfortunately, their mum was absolutely terrified and it took a while for her to accept the shelter volunteers, but thankfully as the puppies started getting more independent and venturing out of their kennel on their own, they were much more sociable and keen to engage with people.

It took a little while to work on their confidence, but they’re all doing so well and are now ready to find their new homes.

Jessie is the most confident of her siblings and she’s always the first to lead the way for her brothers and sisters. She’s brave, inquisitive and playful, and she’s the most likely to investigate a new environment or unfamiliar toy first.

She is friendly, silly and affectionate, and once she’s made friends with you she really loves your company. She’s eager to interact with new people and given a little time to adjust, we think she will absolutely shine in a new home.

Jessie is playful and friendly with other dogs, and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

We also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home, and although it might take her a little longer to adapt, with patience and understanding she will be okay.

Jessie’s ideal home would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city, who they can dedicate time to training and socialising.

Her balanced temperament at her young age is really promising and we think she’s going to grow into an amazing dog with a very human oriented nature.

Each of the pups will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Jessie has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be suitable to live alongside slightly older children, as she can still sometimes be a little skittish, but she really does enjoy the attention.

She loves to play with anything that squeaks, chew on a rope toy or lollop after a ball, and she would be best suited to a moderately active lifestyle.

name: Fred
description:
Fred is a 9 year old male Golden Retriever Cross.

Our poor golden retriever beauty, Fred, was surrendered to the shelter days before his ninth birthday, after spending his entire life being owned.

Unfortunately, his family wouldn’t let him live indoors and refused to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate him living outdoors (which is legal in Cyprus), and veterinary services ended up getting involved.

Fred was extremely stressed when he was brought into the shelter and we’ve spent the last few weeks getting to know him and realising how much he’s actually missed out on over the years.

He may have had a family, but he has had minimal socialisation, very little training, no one to rely on and a lot of instability. In fact, three years ago we actually found Fred miles away from home.

He’d been living on a picnic site for weeks before he was reunited with his family via his microchip.

So now, in his senior years, Fred needs an entirely new beginning. He is looking for a patient, understanding and confident family who recognise that he needs time to adapt.

Although he’s nine years old, he’s very active, strong and bouncy, especially when he gets overexcited. He is therefore not suitable for a home with young children as he has no concept of his size and strength.

Being part retriever, Fred is absolutely obsessed with food. He knows how to sit, and he also offers a very gentle and polite paw, but he inhales his food and any kind of treat is welcome!

He also loves water and loves splashing around in the paddling pool on a hot day. And despite his older age, he’s really still a puppy at heart.

He loves his toys, especially a teddy that he can rip apart as he loves taking the stuffing out of things. He also enjoys playing tug with a rope toy, and chasing after a ball (although he’s not sure on the concept of fetch).

Fred hasn’t been very well socialised with other dogs and this is an area that needs some continued work. He is generally good with females, but the first time we introduced him to other dogs we could see in his body language that he just had no idea what to do.

He’s had very limited interactions with other dogs sadly, so he’s not ready to just go into any home and mingle with lots of resident dogs.

Fred does bond quickly with people though and responds really well to kindness. He is a silly, goofy boy with a huge heart and ultimately all he wants is to be adored. He loves a belly rub, he loves playing, and he is sociable and friendly.

He is looking for a family who recognise that he’s been let down over the years and needs a little more guidance, patient and understanding. There is SO much love in this dog, and in the right home he will absolutely blossom.

name: Gaia
description:
Gaia is a four month old cross-breed. Gaia’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gaia was very shy when she arrived at the shelter and would hang back inside her kennel rather than coming out to say hi. She was very suspicious of new people, and after their rough start it made complete sense for her to be wary.

After a few weeks, and a lot of treats, we managed to reassure Gaia that we were okay to be trusted, and since then she’s never looked back!

Gaia is now a cuddly, silly, goofy and playful puppy who is so much happier than before. She has no issues being held or cuddled, and she welcomes a fuss from new people with little hesitation.

She’s not the loudest or the most front and centre of the litter, but there’s a quiet confidence about her and that will only continue to grow in a home where she has lots of focus and love.

Gaia is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Gaia would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and she’ll really enjoy the opportunity to engage in basic training, as she’s very switched on.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gaia has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be happy living with them, although would prefer a little more predictability, so school age children might be more suitable.

She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties! But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend.

Gaia is a gorgeous young dog and has all the makings of a loyal best friend.

name: Gilly
description:
Gilly is a four month old cross-breed. Gilly’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gilly is such a cutie and has a really joyful energy about her that makes it impossible not to love her. She gets so excited to spend time with people, and she gives so many kisses!

She’s also quite happy worming her way into your lap for a little rest while she takes in everything going on around her – she just loves being involved.

Gilly is a clever girl and is quick to learn new things. She has pretty much learned to sit for a treat already, and although she’s a bit suspicious of the lead at the moment she’s started to trust that it’s not a bad thing anymore.

She has an every wagging tail and a very happy personality, and as she’s very sociable we’re sure it won’t take long for her to make plenty of new friends!

Gilly is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gilly has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a super little character and we know she’s going to make someone very happy!

name: Grant
description:
Grant is a four month old cross-breed. Grant’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

At a glance, Grant looks just as confident as his siblings. He’s always at the bars of the kennel jumping up to meet new people with his brothers and sisters, and the fact that he’s the only pup in the litter with huge ears also draws a lot of attention to him.

However, Grant is actually the most nervous of the pups. As soon as he’s separated from his siblings, he is very unsure of what to do.

He is such a sweet, soft and gentle boy, and he just needs a slightly more patient, calm and understanding home who can go at his pace. We’ve seen so many pups like Grant in our time and the power of the perfect home cannot be underestimated!

Grant is a submissive boy and he’s always a little unsure around new people until he knows that they’re going to treat him with kindness.

When he gets to know you, he likes to just sit beside you and chill, and he loves an ear scratch or a belly rub.

He’s not confident on the lead yet so that will take a bit of work, but there’s not a bad bone in his body and he really does want to trust people, he just takes a little longer than his siblings.

Grant would be better suited to a home with another resident dog that he can learn from and play with. As soon as he’s away from his siblings, he panics and is visibly less confident.

Another dog would definitely help his transition from shelter to sofa, and help him feel less overwhelmed and confused.

The ideal home for Grant would be a loving, patient family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city.

As Grant is more nervous than his siblings, a calm home in a quieter area would be great for him, and we’re sure his confidence will grow once he’s settled and feeling more secure.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grant is just a baby and has never had an adverse reaction to a child, but in order to keep things predictable for him we’re looking for a home with older children only.

He just needs some time and understanding to come out of his shell, and he’s only a few months old right now – he will change so much within the first few months of his adoption and it will simply take a special, caring family to give him the love and support he needs.

We’re already seeing glimpses of the silly, charming and playful little pup he is, and it will be so rewarding to see him really flourish with his new family.

name: Gina
description:
Gina is a four month old cross breed. Gina’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gina is very confident among the group and can be a bit bossy with her siblings! She is a girl who knows what she wants, and sometimes that is the limelight!

She is always very eager to say hello to passing visitors that walk by her kennel, and she loves any opportunity to be be cuddled or played with.

She also loves chasing after a toy, a pebble or a stick – it doesn’t matter what it is, she can make a game out of anything!

Gina isn’t familiar with the lead just yet, but she’s starting to learn that it’s a positive thing now. She is super excitable and bouncy when she gets the chance to interact with people, and she bonds fiercely with those that she loves.

She is definitely going to be a very loyal companion, we have no doubt about that.

Gina is good with other dogs and on the most part she gets along well with her siblings, but she needs a bit of work on sharing. She could definitely live alongside a resident dog, and an older, calmer dog would be a great influence on her.

However, we also think she is confident enough to be the only dog in the household.

The ideal home for Gina would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and of course being a puppy she will both enjoy and benefit from some introductory training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gina has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be great for a family with school age children. She can be a bit nippy in her play, but that is purely to do with her age.

She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Given the opportunity, we know Gina is going to grow up into a lovely young dog with a great personality and nothing but devotion for her new family.

name: Godfrey
description:
Godfrey is a four month old cross-breed. Godfrey’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Godfrey is a sweetheart and it took us a little bit longer to earn his trust than some of his siblings. The girls are definitely more confident than their brothers in this litter!

Once Godfrey realised that he was safe, he ventured out to explore his new surroundings and he has been quite taken with the toys, the paddling pool (or the water bowl if the pool isn’t filled!) and the fact that so many treats are on offer! He’s realised it’s not so bad after all.

Godfrey is really cute when he gets to spend some 1-2-1 time with the volunteers, and he really enjoys being the centre of attention for a little while.

Although you can tell he’s a little unsure, he revels in the fuss and loves being cuddled and tickled. He’s a very loving little dog and once his initial nerves have subsided he’s quite the snuggler, and he also gives excellent kisses.

He’s not familiar with the lead just yet, but when he’s outside in the yard sniffing about he’s very curious about other dogs, and bravely approaches to give them a little sniff before running back to safety! He’s also one of the smaller pups of the litter.

Godfrey is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that he can learn from and play with.

He’s a very friendly boy and reads other dogs very well, and we think he would probably prefer a home with another dog, but we’re open to considering placing him on his own if we think it’s the right fit.

The ideal home for Godfrey would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. He would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and he would also do well with some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Godfrey has had some initial exposure to children and we think he would be suitable to live alongside slightly older children, as he can still sometimes be a little skittish.

He is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if he’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Godfrey is such a little heartbreaker and we know that someone isn’t going to be able to stop themselves falling in love with his charming little face – and we don’t blame you!

name: Grace
description:
Grace is a four month old cross-breed. Grace’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Grace is one of the most confident pups in the litter, and even within the first couple of days after she arrived in the shelter she has been brave enough to approach new people, interact and cuddle.

Some of the other pups follow her lead as she’s a very sociable little thing and loves to be in the company of people. She warms to anyone and everyone very quickly and is definitely ready to find a family of her own.

Grace is very food motivated and was the first of the litter to learn ‘sit’. She is also accepting of the lead, which can sometimes be a bit scary for new puppies to adapt to, but she’s taken everything in her stride and learns new things fast.

She loves a belly rub, any excuse to be as close to you as possible, and she’s also very playful – the perfect all rounder!

Grace is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with. She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Grace would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grace has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a wonderful young dog and we can’t wait to find her the perfect family to grow up with.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie is a two year old Pointer mix who was found as a stray and had been hiding in abandoned buildings across open farmland for a while before she was able to be caught.

The vet confirmed she had not been microchipped, and as she’d been roaming for a while it was clear she’d not come from a home.

She was rescued from agricultural land where strays are often found, and unsurprisingly, no one came to the shelter to claim her as their own.

Bonnie arrived just after Christmas and has been in the shelter without any interest ever since. She was absolutely terrified when she first arrived, and was so avoidant of people.

She didn’t want anyone to touch her, and would hide in the back of her kennel when anyone approached. She was then paired up with a confident male dog who has zero fear of anyone or anything, and slowly she started to realise that she was safe.

Bonnie is now a different dog. She’s still a little bit reserved and needs time to trust new people, but she’s much more friendly, so much happier, and she’s really come out of her shell in the past few months.

She is more confident in the company of other dogs, and she’s really benefitted from having a kennel friend to learn from and follow their lead. This in mind, we think she would be better suited to a home with another calm, resident dog.

Bonnie would struggle in a loud home in a busy area, so we’re looking for a laid-back home atmosphere based in a calmer residential, or semi-rural location.

She would love to be surrounded by fields and nature walks, rather than roads and buildings, and she is definitely looking for a home with direct access to a secure garden.

We know that given the time she needs, and a gentle, patient approach, Bonnie will absolutely blossom and she’ll make an amazing companion with a little time and understanding.

Bonnie has had some introductory lead training, and has responded well, but still needs a bit more work. She is a relatively active dog and would welcome long walks, but is also quite happy basking in the sun on a warm day.

Given that she’s a shyer dog, we are looking for a home with children aged 8+, so as not to overwhelm her. There’s not a bad bone in her body, but she’d struggle with a very unpredictable household, and would prefer a calm home.

Bonnie absolutely deserves a second chance and we know that given the patience that she needs, she will do so well in a new home.

She spent a long time in survival mode, so she just needs a secure environment to understand that she doesn’t have to look out for herself all the time – she’ll be treated with kindness, love and affection.

She’s already grown in confidence and made great progress in the shelter, so in a proper home she’s going to do just fine.

name: Jasmine
description:
Our extra special girl Jasmine is approximately one year old and a delightful small cross breed. Jasmine weighs a humble seven kilos and measures eleven inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Jasmine has been in our Cyprus shelter for three weeks.

Jasmine is stunningly attractive. She has incredibly delicate features and the most beautiful facial expressions. This blends so well with her bubbly and fun-loving disposition.

Jasmine’s coat and markings are sublime. She has some classic black and tan with a distinctive white flash to her chest. And then there’s the gorgeous half tone brindle along her back. If ever a dog were to stand out from the crowd it would be Jasmine.
