She is youthful, fun loving, affable and affectionate. Jasmine so yearns for human interaction and will make a glorious family dog.

Jasmine will benefit from more lead training but so enjoys her time in the car. She seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs and children but has a strong desire to chase cats.

name: Frank
description:
Frank is a 9-week-old male Presa Canario. He is a handsome puppy who has enjoyed the very best start in life after being born at Ravenswood alongside his brothers and sisters.

Having spent his early weeks in a caring environment, he has been given every opportunity to grow into a happy and confident young dog.

From an early age, Frank has been well socialised and regularly handled, helping him become comfortable around people and everyday interactions.

He has also been wormed routinely as part of his early care, ensuring he has received the attention every puppy deserves.

As a cheerful and confident puppy, Frank is now ready to find a loving forever home.

Because he is a Presa Canario, he will need owners who have previous experience with large breeds and understand the commitment involved in raising such a powerful dog.

His new family should be prepared to continue his socialisation and training throughout his life. Ongoing guidance, positive reinforcement, and consistent handling will help Frank develop into a well-mannered and balanced adult.

Presa Canarios are large, strong dogs that thrive with knowledgeable owners who are willing to invest time and effort into their upbringing.

Anyone considering Frank should be confident in providing the structure, training, and lifestyle that a breed of this size requires.

Frank has already received his first vaccination and has been microchipped before leaving for his new home. He will also need to be neutered when he is old enough, and his future owners will be required to provide proof that this has been carried out.

Frank is looking for a permanent home where he can continue to learn, grow, and become a valued member of the family.

If you believe you can offer this handsome young Presa Canario the loving and committed home he deserves, he would be delighted to meet you.

name: Jordan
description:
Jordan is a three year old Pointer mix. He’s super shiny, super sleek, this gorgeous boy is Jordan He arrived at the shelter along with two other pointers, all of whom were found roaming as strays at the end of the hunting season.

The three of them are happy in each other’s company, and now they share a kennel together. As their individual personalities have emerged we’ve been getting to know them, and now we would love to find each of them their perfect forever home.

Jordan is around three years old and such a nice boy! Unfortunately, we don’t think that Jordan has experienced the kindest treatment throughout his life, and it has meant that it’s taken us a little more time to convince him that we’re to be trusted.

He has however responded so well to reassurance and kindness, and is now much more confident and sociable. He now really likes going out for little walks with the shelter volunteers, and he always looks to them for a bit of guidance or a cuddle.

Around other dogs, Jordan is really friendly. He is a bit of a goon and loves to play, but he’s also friendly and gentle, especially when meeting new dogs.

He is good with both males and females, and we definitely think that he would really enjoy a home where he had another resident dog to learn from and play with.

Having another dog to observe and learn from will allow Jordan to adapt at his own pace, and with someone to look up to, to boost his confidence.

Jordan would be best suited to a semi-rural home where he’s surrounded by lots of places to explore. Being a pointer, he loves to follow his nose and he’s always curious about his surroundings.

He would also be best suited to a home with a garden, as it’s likely that he has spent the vast majority of his life living outdoors in some capacity.

A garden will provide Jordan with a safe outdoor space where he can acclimatise to living indoors little by little.

Jordan has already started to show us that when he trusts someone he is super affectionate and sweet, and given proper time to bond with a new family we know that he is going to develop a really strong, loyal connection with them.

Pointers are such fantastic companions and given the opportunity to settle into a secure and loving environment, we know Jordan will really blossom in confidence.

name: Indie
description:
Indie is a three year old Shepherd mix who was brought into the shelter after locals notified the dog warden that she had been roaming freely around the village for a few weeks.

No one seemed to know where she’d come from, or was able to advise who she belonged to. With no microchip to help us connect the dots she ended up in the shelter, and is now waiting for a new home.

Indie is a beautiful girl who just blends in at the shelter.

She doesn’t ask for much, she doesn’t demand attention, and she shares her kennel with two very silly male dogs who she is extremely tolerant and gentle with, despite their complete lack of spatial awareness or manners!

She is very patient with other dogs and gets on well with them, but equally would be fine to be homed as the only resident dog, as she’s quietly confident and independent.

Indie is a very clever girl and loves her treats. As she’s food motivated this will really help with any further training her new family might want to do with her, as she responds really well to positive reinforcement.

It’s likely that Indie is a shepherd mix, so she will enjoy training, enrichment and brain games, as dogs like her thrive with focus and direction.

The ideal home for Indie would be an active family who can offer her plenty of opportunities to explore and are looking for a loyal, devoted companion to accompany them on their adventures.

Indie bonds with new people quickly and is a very loving dog, so we think she will adapt to a companion lifestyle well.

Indie would be happiest in a semi-rural setting where she’s surrounded by nice places to walk, fields to roam through or woods to wander in.

She would welcome trips to the beach or long hikes at the weekend, and she will be able to keep up with a more active pace of life. We’re sure she’ll be very excited to experience home comforts as well though!

We don’t know if Indie has ever had the opportunity to have her own bed or even live indoors before, so her family need to be patient while she adjusts in her own time. For anyone looking for a loyal best friend, Indie would be perfect.

name: Nala
description:
Nala is a 9-week-old female Presa Canario. She is a gorgeous puppy who has had the very best start in life after being born at Ravenswood alongside her brothers and sister.

Raised in a caring environment from birth, she has received plenty of attention and care during her early weeks.

Nala has been well socialised and regularly handled, helping her grow into a happy and confident young puppy. She has also been wormed regularly, ensuring she has received the routine care needed as she prepares for life with her new family.

As she begins her search for a forever home, Nala will need owners who have experience with large breed dogs.

Presa Canarios are powerful dogs that require knowledgeable owners who understand their needs and are committed to providing the right guidance.

Her new family should be prepared to continue her socialisation and training throughout her life. Consistent training and positive experiences will help Nala develop into a well-mannered and confident adult dog.

Because Presa Canarios are large and strong, they thrive in homes where their owners are ready to take on the responsibilities that come with the breed. A patient and committed approach will give Nala the best opportunity to reach her full potential.

Nala has already received her first vaccination and has been microchipped before leaving for her new home. She will also need to be neutered when she is old enough, and her new owners will be required to provide proof that this has been completed.

Nala is ready to start the next chapter of her life with a loving family that can offer her a secure and permanent home.

If you believe you can provide the care, commitment, and lifelong support she needs, Nala would love to find her forever home with you.

name: Zayla
description:
Zayla is a 9-week-old female Presa Canario. She is a gorgeous puppy who has enjoyed the very best start in life after being born at Ravenswood alongside her brothers and sister.

Having been raised in a caring environment from birth, she has benefited from excellent early care and attention.

During her first weeks of life, Zayla has been well socialised and regularly handled, helping her become a happy and confident young puppy.

She has also been wormed routinely, ensuring she has received the care needed during these important early stages of development.

Now ready to find her forever home, Zayla is looking for owners who understand the needs of large breed dogs. As a Presa Canario, she will require a home with previous large breed experience and people who are committed to helping her reach her full potential.

Her new family should continue her socialisation and provide consistent training throughout her life. Ongoing guidance, patience, and positive reinforcement will help her mature into a well-balanced and well-behaved adult dog.

Presa Canarios are powerful, strong dogs that thrive with confident and responsible owners who are prepared for the commitment that comes with the breed.

Zayla will benefit from a home that is ready to provide the structure, leadership, and lifelong training she needs.

Before leaving for her new home, Zayla has received her first vaccination and has been microchipped. She will also need to be neutered when she is old enough, and her new owners will be required to provide proof that this has been completed.

Zayla is ready to begin the next chapter of her life with a family that can offer her love, stability, and the ongoing support she deserves.

If you feel you can provide this beautiful Presa Canario with a permanent and caring home, she would love to meet you.

name: Peanut
description:
Peanut is a four month old female cross-breed puppy, and she and her siblings were brought into the shelter as an abandoned litter when they were just a month old.

They were so tiny, they looked like baby otters – just piles of fluff that napped on each other for the majority of the day. As the pups got older, more playful and independent, one by one they were adopted locally.

Unfortunately, Peanut is now the only one left behind. All her brothers and sisters have left, and she’s been adopted into another litter of new arrivals so she’s not alone.

We would love to find her forever home now and give her the chance her siblings have had.

Peanut is never the loudest of the bunch or the first puppy to come dashing over to you. She’s a little more reserved and sensitive, and sometimes a little unsure around new people.

She was always used to her siblings stealing the limelight while she hung back, so when she does get some 1-2-1 attention she realises just how great it is and suddenly has a burst of excitement!

Peanut has spent some time with children around the age of eight, and she absolutely loved them. She was a tiny but shy to start with, but then climbed into their laps and gave them loads of kisses.

She was loving all the attention and cuddles, and we think that she would be a lovely addition to a home with gentle kids.

Around other dogs Peanut just makes friends with everyone. Because she is a more submissive character she can sometimes get trampled or bullied, but she’s learning to hold her own and stand her ground!

She has integrated alongside multiple new puppies that have arrived during her time, and she’s made friends with them all. She’s playful, loves a bit of rough and tumble, and likes having company to snuggle up with at nap time.

She would be great with another resident dog and would learn so much from having a confident company to follow in the footsteps of.

Peanut would be best suited to a calm household with a moderately active lifestyle and access to a garden. She needs reassurance, patient and time as she is adapting to a companion lifestyle.

This will be a very new concept for her, as she’s never lived in a home before. And as with any puppies, she will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Peanut has the sweetest, most charming personality and it’s so sad that she’s been left behind, but perhaps they’ve left the best til last!

name: Billy
description:
Billy is a smallish crossbreed aged around three years old. Billy fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Billy was found outside the gates of the Crivatu private shelter in Romania around a year or so ago and pretty much invited himself inside. He has lived happily there until recently joining us in the UK to look for his forever home.

Billy is a cute little “man about town” kind of guy with a lot of character. Secretly he’s quite sensitive and insecure with new people and new situations but he “styles it out” with an air of nonchalance initially.

A couple of days later when he realises he’s in safe hands he is your best and most loyal friend. Billy loves a fuss and a cuddle, he’s enjoying his walks and loving being a domestic house dog.

Billy gets on well with other dogs and would like another dog companion in his forever home ideally but would settle as the only dog in the home with a little extra time too. He is living happily with a cat currently and would like an adult home environment.

name: Harper
description:
Harper is a small to medium sized female crossbreed aged 18 month old.

Harper had a start in life that is sadly all too common in her native country of Romania. She was taken into the Botosani public shelter at a very young age as one of hundreds of puppies that get dumped there each year and she simply didn’t get picked for adoption.

So many waste what is supposed to be care free puppy time living in the stress and filth of the shelter. They grow up not knowing anything other than what is contained in the depravation of their pen.

Harper has recently arrived in her uk foster home. She has been for her first walk, set her feet on grass for the first time and is tip toeing her way through so many other new and daunting experiences for the very first time.

She’s bright and alert and picking everything up at a rapid pace and we desperately hope we can find her a family that will continue to show her both the simple pleasures in life and the love she has been missing since birth.

Harper mixes well with other dogs and will need another confidant companion dog in her forever home. She is already showing a fun and cheeky character and just needs to continue gaining experience and confidence. She could live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Ben
description:
Ben is a medium sized (overweight) male crossbreed aged around seven to eight years old. Ben is fostered in Mattishall Norfolk.

Ben was on a kill list at a public shelter in Romania when a lady in the UK offered to take him.

Unfortunately, Ben was unhandled and the lady was not prepared or experienced enough to cope with his rehabilitation and so we were asked to go and get him and enter upon that journey with him.

It’s taken several months but Ben is now ready to move on. He still has the annoying habit of chewing through his lead if not watched carefully hence the metal lead in the pics!

Other than that he’s actually emerging into a sweet old boy who has even begun to casually ask for fuss and attention.

His love for food helps to win his trust and confidence but at some time soon his diet and exercise regime are going to have to be addressed. This will be secondary to becoming friends though.

Ben mixes well with other dogs and would like at least one other dog in his forever home. He really can’t be bothered with the cat.

He will need someone patient to win his trust but after a few weeks he has the potential to be a comical and loving companion. At this point effort will need to be made to retrieve the waistline I’m sure he once had

If you like a dog with a bit of quirk and character and appreciate a little stubbornness chucked into the mix for good measure then Ben is the boy for you.

He won’t love you overnight but you’ll enjoy the challenge of getting to that point with him and treasure the bond even more. He will need an adult family with someone with a reasonable level of experience.

name: Jack
description:
Jack is a 7-8 years old medium sized crossbreed.

Blue eyed Jack used to belong to a family who kept him in a 2×2 pen. Not on a chain but never walked, never socialized. Then at some point they got bored with him and wanted to get a terra nova or something similar to replace him with.

A neighbour took Jack, but could not keep him since she already had a lot of dogs. So he was moved to a private shelter where he stayed for close to two years and where we visited him on two previous trips. He’s an absolute sweetheart.

Jack is now looking for his forever home. Jack can be strong on lead as he loves his walks.

He gets on ok with other dogs but would prefer to live with a calmer female or as an only dog. Jack really likes children and could live with respectful children aged seven plus.

Jack enjoys structure and routine and would be particularly good at something like agility or hoopers.

Have you got a place in your heart for this blue eyed boy?

name: Cathy
description:
Cathy is a 9 month old pup who we think will grow to be medium sized but parentage is unknown.

Cathy has come into our care recently from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. She is one of the less confident amongst the puppy craziness currently, but given just a little time and she is the sweetest and loving little girl.

Puppies need someone at home for a large part of the day. They can make noise, mess and chew up your stuff until they are trained not to do so and we really don’t like it when puppies get returned for simply being puppies so please consider this carefully before applying.

Needs a resident dog in her forever home.

name: Bobbin
description:
Bobbin is a medium sized crossbreed aged around two years old.

Bobbin was a puppy in the Botosani public shelter in Romania and tragically he never got picked and therefore grew up there. The filthy concrete floors and metal bars are all he’s ever known until he recently traveled to his UK foster home.

Bobbin is having an absolute blast in his new surroundings. Following his foster mum around and learning new things by the minute. He is initially a little shy with strangers as he’s not seen much of people previously but it doesn’t take long at all to win his trust.

He is now living the puppyhood he was so tragically deprived of and playing all day long. His tail never stops wagging.

Bobbin mixes very well with dogs and needs a resident dog in his forever home. He wants to play with the cat and give him kisses, but soon submits when the cat puts him firmly in his place. Bobbin could live with respectful children aged 10 plus.

name: Matteo
description:
Matteo is a medium/large crossbreed aged around four years old.

Matteo has come into our care recently from Roxana’s shelter in Romania. He went into the shelter as a puppy along with his mum and sister and sadly grew up there.

Matteo is a comical character who is adapting well to his new life but still has a lot of new experiences to encounter. He has a whole catalog of facial expressions that make us smile.

He is not very brave when encountering new things but after a few repeats of them he loses his fears and is really starting to enjoy and be fascinated by life outside of the shelter.

He gets on well with other dogs and would like to live with at least one other dog in his forever home. He can live with respectful children aged ten plus.

He will need patience and guidance while he builds up confidence out in the big wide world. He is affectionate and cheeky with people he knows well and will make a fab addition to his lucky new family.

name: Sherman
description:
Sherman is a 10 month old pup who we think will grow to be medium sized but parentage is unknown.

We met Sherman in our last trip to Botosani public shelter in Romania. He is one of the less confident pups so we would need an adopter who has time and patience to settle him in his new environment.

He could live with or without resident dogs and would be suitable for children 12+.

He will need all the usual training and care that all pups need and adopters should expect peeing, poohing, chewing and potentially sleepless nights until work is put into training them out of it.

name: Hattie
description:
Meet Hattie a 3 year old small size kokoni cross girl.

She is now thriving in a wonderful foster home near Oxford, where she lives happily with other dogs who have helped her discover that life can be fun, safe and full of kindness.

Every day she grows a little more confident, and more of her sweet, playful personality begins to show.

Hattie’s early life wasn’t easy. She was one of 27 dogs rescued from a hoarding situation, where she had very little socialisation or positive human contact.

When she first came into rescue, the world felt overwhelming and trusting people seemed impossible.

She chooses to spend time near her foster family, enjoys relaxing with her doggy friends and is learning that people can be kind. Every little milestone has taken courage, which makes her progress all the more special.

Hattie will need at least one friendly, confident resident dog in her forever home. Other dogs give her reassurance, help her understand new situations and show her that the world is not such a frightening place.

She will not be the sort of dog who settles in overnight, so she needs patient adopters who are willing to let her take life at her own pace. Ideally, she is looking for a calm home where her people have the time to help her continue building her confidence.

Right now, Hattie is happiest playing with her doggy friends and relaxing at home. As her confidence grows, we hope she will begin to enjoy countryside walks and exploring with her forever family.

The most rewarding part of adopting Hattie will be watching her develop over the weeks and months ahead, seeing her discover that she is safe and knowing that you helped make that possible.

One day, the timid little dog you welcomed into your home may quietly become your shadow and the most loyal companion you could wish for.

A home with at least one friendly, confident resident dogA calm home with people who can dedicate time to helping her settlePatient, understanding adopters who will let her develop at her own paceA secure and loving home where she can continue to blossom

Could you be the person to give Hattie the future she deserves?

name: Molly
description:
Molly is a medium to large sized crossbreed aged around three years old. Molly fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Molly was rescued from a sheep field in Romania when she was a puppy. The shepherd called a known rescuer and said that he was going to “get rid”of all the dogs because there were too many.

When rescuers went for them they were all tied very tightly in a sealed cardboard box. One of the pups was even tied at the muzzle. They were seconds away from suffocation.

Molly and two of her sisters were not lucky enough to get adopted as pups and so grew up in the private shelter. Safe and loved but in a pen not experiencing the joys of their own home. Molly is now in a UK foster home waiting awaiting an adoption offer.

Molly is a happy and affectionate girl, she’s a little hesitant in new situations so will just need further socialisation.

She mixes well with the other dogs in her foster home and will need another dog as full time resident in her forever home . She could live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Floyd
description:
Floyd is a medium sized crossbreed aged three to four years old. Floyd fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Floyd was rescued from a kill shelter in Romania when he was just three months old. Sadly he never got a home offer and has spent all of his life in a shelter environment.

Floyd is a cheeky and smiley boy who always makes us smile. He’s a little hand shy simply through lack of time spent with him over the years to offer actual human contact.

He’s very happy to be around his people though and gives the most enthusiastic happy dance greetings you’ll ever see. Floyd enjoys the company of other dogs and will need another resident dog in his forever home.

He could live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Rox
description:
Rox is a medium sized crossbreed aged around 13 months old. Rox fostered North Walsham Norfolk.

Rox and her sister Ree were found in the middle of nowhere in Romania, near a road, obviously abandoned, without food, water, or shelter.

It was last summer, when temperatures were soaring outside. They were taken by the Animal Police and brought to Roxana’s shelter.

When Rox first arrived with us, she was a shy girl who found the world a little overwhelming. Since then, we’ve watched her grow in confidence day by day, revealing her gentle, loving side.

Her journey hasn’t been without challenges. She spent several weeks undergoing two operations to correct hip dysplasia, but she faced every hurdle with quiet determination and has now made a full recovery.

Her vet is delighted with her progress and expects her to live a normal, active life without any further complications.

She has a wonderfully gentle nature and has settled beautifully into her foster home, where she gets on very well with her foster pack.

While she can be cautious around new people at first, with a little patience and kindness she soon learns to trust and her affectionate personality begins to shine through.

As Rox’s confidence has grown, so has her love for human company. She absolutely adores being close to her people and gives the best face licks!

Once she forms a bond, her loyalty has been unwavering, and loves nothing more than spending time with those she trusts.

Because of her early hip issues, she had a slower start when it came to exploring the world, but she is now gaining confidence on her walks and enjoying new experiences more and more each day.

She will need a patient and understanding adopter who is willing to give her the time she needs to settle in and build trust. In return, they will be rewarded with one of the most loving, gentle, and loyal dogs imaginable.

Rox mixes well with the other dogs in her foster home and we would prefer another dog as full time resident in her forever home although this is not essential.

She could live with respectful children aged 12 plus.

name: Desmond
description:
Desmond is a medium sized crossbreed who is coming up to two years old. Desmond fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Desmond was taken into the Botosani public shelter as a pup, nobody remembers who took him there or why. Sadly he didn’t get picked for adoption so he grew up there.

The day that the puppies there get transferred from the puppy block to the adult block is a very depressing day indeed, their chances of ever leaving decrease significantly on that short walk across the shelter.

Desmond was pointed out to us as one of last years pups when we visited in October last year. He joined our “future dogs” list and has recently joined us here in the UK.

It’s been a lot for him to get used to when he’s never seen outside of the shelter walls, but he’s learning and he’s opening up to the new adventures.

Desmond is a sweet boy who is initially wary of new people and will need a few weeks to fully connect with his new family. He’s an amiable chap and gets on great with the other dogs.

He was initially shocked at the introduction of a new species when he met the safe rescue cat and avoided looking at him unless he was sure that the cat was looking the other way.

He would need at least one other dog to continue to show him the ropes in his forever home. Desmond could live with respectful children aged twelve plus.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a large crossbreed female aged around ten years old. Freya fostered Kings Lynn Norfolk.

She was found in bushes in Crivatu Romania a few years ago and was taken to the private shelter nearby.

She is a calm and steady girl who still enjoys short walks. She mixes well with all dogs but is quite a dominant member of the pack.

She keeps all the youngsters at the shelter in check with a firm but fair approach and they all love and respect her for that. She could also live happily as the only dog in the home.

Freya is an affectionate and loyal companion who would suit someone with large breed experience who can pamper her in her twilight years. She would be ok with respectful children aged twelve plus.

name: Stanley
description:
Stanley is a small to medium sized crossbreed, he is probably around nine years old.

Stanley came into our care four years ago from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. He had been extremely picked on in the shelter and was very underweight due to other dogs not allowing him to eat.

Far from being grateful to us for stepping in and saving him from impending doom, it’s fair to say that Stanley has never really been a “people person”. After years of hardship at the hands of humans we never really blamed him.

So we’ve been ticking along for four years feeding him, picking up his pooh and receiving nothing in gratitude but dirty looks. All that mattered was that he was out of the shelter and happy and safe in his foster home.

For the duration of his stay with us he’s really not been any trouble at all. He blends into the background for the most part. Will tolerate me bathing and grooming him without a fuss when needed. He’s just never really shown any sign of wanting any further interaction.

Recently I have felt a change in him, I would even go as far as to say that he almost forgot himself yesterday and enjoyed a groom and a fuss!

When he rested his head on my knee and dozed off I suddenly realised that actually he’s really a senior now and he deserves a quieter and more relaxed environment for his retirement.

Obviously he needs a very special kind of person to offer him a home. It is still potentially going to be a case of what you can do for him and not what love he’s going to give back to you.….. but just maybe in a more one to one environment he can be more than a “blend into the background” dog. In the meantime rewards will be from offering comfort and peace to a stoic old boy who just wants to use you for food!!

Stanley needs another dog in residence and can be playful when he thinks nobody is looking, he has no issues with cats. He has been in a foster home with children of eight plus, he ignores them and they ignore him and that situation works for all involved.

He will go for walks and enjoys them initially but gets belligerent after about twenty minutes, especially if you opt to go in a direction which displeases him.

I just think that you can see in the eyes of this dog that he’s seen and endured way more than any dog should, and he should therefore not be judged for his standoffish approach to humans. During grooming sessions I’ve seen the scars hidden by his thick coat, and they are many.

name: Cristina
description:
Cristina is a medium to large sized crossbreed, born March 2023.

Cristina was rescued as a pup from the streets of Crevedia in Romania. She came to the UK September 2023 and was quickly adopted but was returned after a few weeks because she didn’t have a good relationship with the man in that household.

Cristina was cared for by a man in Romania and there is also a man in her current foster home, both of which she gets on well with.

Cristina lived with a cat and a small child in that home and loved playing with them but sometimes got “a bit much” as she’s clumsy and enthusiastic.

She is a sweet and loyal girl with those she loves. She would benefit from one to one training to curb that enthusiasm, but we quite like her zest for life!

She is a leggy, clutzy, lovable fool who just needs a little time invested in her. She loves her walks and is well behaved out and about but can be wary of people she doesn’t know entering her home.

Cristina is loving playing with the other dogs in her foster but would need any other dog or dogs in the household to be confident as she’d be too much for a more reserved character.

She but could live as an only dog if sufficiently exercised and stimulated.

Cristina needs an experienced owner, she’s a lot but she’s also great fun and so comical. She’s not for everyone but for the right person she’s going to be that dog you never ever forget.

name: Mr. Bean
description:
Mr. Bean is a medium sized crossbreed aged around two and a half years old.

Mr. Bean arrived at the Botosani public with his mum and siblings when he was a tiny pup. The rest of his family all got adopted but he wasn’t chosen and so he was left to grow up in the shelter. He is now in a UK foster home and learning about life out side of a pen.

Mr. Bean is a comical character whose natural curiosity is carrying him through all the lessons he has to learn to catch up on what most dogs would learn from a much younger age. He is super keen to please and will simply need to gain experience when he moves to his forever home.

He gets on brilliantly with other dogs and having a canine companion would really help him to have around in his forever home, he could be the only dog with a little more time and patience from his adoptive family. My. Bean could live with respectful children aged eight plus. He is a delightful character who deserves all the love in the world now that he’s finally out of the shelter.

name: Pettern
description:
Pettern is a medium sized crossbreed born June 2022.

Pettern was abandoned with his siblings outside the gates of the shelter in Crivatu, Romania. Sadly they grew up in there whilst waiting for their chance to come to the UK to find a new home.

Pettern is a sweet, affectionate, playful and loyal boy to his family but is a bit of a wimp when it comes to meeting strangers. He was adopted once as an only dog but really didn’t cope so will need another dog in full time residence in his forever home.

He is fine with the safe rescue cat, actually he’s a bit intimidated by him too.

Pettern is super loyal and loving, he is good on and off lead. He will need an adult home environment. He loves toys and is very playful with the dogs in his foster home.

name: Levi
description:
Levi is a medium sized crossbreed born in Feb 2023.

Levi came to us at six months old from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. Having been discarded like rubbish as a baby, he spent his first weeks and months in the squalid conditions there with little to no human interaction.

When he arrived in the UK he was terrified of humans and it took several weeks to get him to the point where he was ready to find his forever home. Since his album went up he’s had no enquiries and has sadly grown up in our care.

Levi is now a fun loving boy who enjoys being around people he knows well. He is cheeky and playful with us but still very unsure strangers due to his past.

Levi loves to play with the other dogs in his foster home and will need a reasonably playful companion in his new home. We would not consider a home for him that doesn’t already have a resident dog.

He loves his toys and has a wonderful time on walks in local woods. He will be very cautious when anyone comes to see him and so needs someone who can see beyond this to the dog he will one day become.

He really has come such a long way in a short space of time and will continue to thrive with someone willing to give him time, love and sausages.

Levi will need an adult home and is uninterested in the safe rescue cat.

name: Alfie
description:
Alfie is a medium sized crossbreed aged around three years old. Alfie fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Alfie had recently been taken into the Boto?ani public shelter in Romania when we visited in March. He was absolutely terrified and completely shut down at the environment he’d been plunged into.

During the days that we were there the team worked with him and by the time we left they were being greeted with happy dances and a wagging tail.

He was booked to come on the first possible transport and is now here in the UK looking for his forever home.

Alfie is a playful and friendly boy who forms strong bonds with his human. He would be best to be the only dog in the home as he can be competitive over toys and food but an experienced adopter could manage him with another dog.

Alfie could live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Mabel
description:
Mabel is a medium sized crossbreed aged around four years old. Mabel fostered Badersfield Norfolk.

Mabel came into our care a few weeks ago from Roxanas shelter in Romania. She was initially found in a nearby village after her and her siblings were abandoned as puppies.

Mabel is a timid and reserved character who has been in her foster home for approximately 12 weeks, making gradual progress.

Initially, she was fearful of human touch, but recently, she has started to enjoy affection and gets excited when she sees familiar faces.

Mabel requires a home with at least one other dog as permanent resident, as she relies heavily on her pack. She loves going for walks, but prefers quieter areas due to her sensitivity to traffic. She could live with respectful children aged twelve plus.

name: Rupert
description:
Rupert is a large golden labrador aged around eight years old.

Rupert has come into our care recently from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. He had been in there for some time along with his three adult sons who are still there.

Rupert is a determined old goat who has probably led a pretty transient life prior to the shelter, used to going as and where he pleases. He found lead training rather a trial and has only now (mostly) accepted that he has to go where the humans direct now.

However he is only going on short walks currently because when he decides he is tired and it’s time to lie down there’s not an awful lot that can be done to persuade him otherwise.

On arrival in his UK foster home he spent the first half day just testing all boundaries to see if there was a way out, when placed in new situations this is a habit that he repeats.

Only when he has proven to himself that he is not super dog and cannot jump five foot fences with his aging bones will he give a big sigh and settle into a pattern of pretty much snoozing most of the day.

He is content with his lot but has to just see first if there’s better on the other side of that fence. It’s not a process that lasts long but seems to be a ritual that can be expected when he’s moved.

Rupert is living happily with other dogs but is quite oblivious to them. He’d be just as happy as the only dog and has been cohabiting happily with the cat and even shares his treats with him.

Despite giving the appearance of a soppy, docile old lab Rupert is not currently approaching for fuss or appreciative of it, although he will allow it and seems neither distressed or scared by it.

I guess if he’s lived this far in his life without the love and kindness of humans the concept of a cuddle is still an enigma to him. He certainly won’t be lying devotedly by your feet or bringing you your slippers anytime soon, but in time and with enough treat bribery who knows?!?

Rupert would like an adult family environment without too much activity for his retirement years.

name: Joey
description:
Joey is a medium sized crossbreed aged around five years old.

Joey was picked up from a killing shelter Mogosoaia, Romania, together with several other dogs right before the transport ban in 2021. He waited in another shelter before moving to Crivatu a couple of years ago. He’s recently come to the UK to look for his forever home.

Joey is timid with strangers and tense about being stroked but he is gradually getting better with people he knows well. A cheeky and comical character is beginning to emerge which will only flourish when he benefits with more one to one attention in his forever home.

Joey will need at least one other confident dog in his new life. He is fine with a confident cat but would like an adult family environment.

name: Colby
description:
Colby is a medium sized crossbreed aged around five years old.

Colby came into our care around a year ago from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. Safe to say he’d been well taught to fear and dislike people from all he’d seen from the human race.

To say he didn’t like us would be an understatement and it was a long time before we could do anything but feed him and just be around him. Over time we gained his trust enough to remove the matted dreadlocks he’d come to us carrying, little by little he grew to love us.

Colby is now one of our favourite characters. He loves to play with the broom when we sweep the floors, he gets the most excited of the whole pack when I come home from the quickest of errands and is beside himself with excitement when I return from my regular trips to Romania.

Colby will need to live with another dog or dogs full time. He will need someone with a good level of experience with nervous dogs who is willing to be patient to earn his trust. I cannot tell you how rewarding he is, you may not see the real him initially but after a few weeks you will be amused and besotted with the dog that will be revealed. He will need an adult home environment.

name: Oscar
description:
Oscar is a small to medium sized whippety shaped crossbreed aged around a year old.

Oscar is fostered in Leamington Spa Warwickshire.

Oscar has had the worst start in life possible. Abandoned at the Botosani public shelter as a tiny puppy by people who never cared for him in the first place. His early weeks spent as one of 150 puppies, none of them being handled, socialised or anything but the most basic of care.

When it came to the day that he was due to travel to us he had contracted a bad dose of kennel cough and he couldn’t travel, meaning more formative weeks spent in much the same way. When he arrived in our care he was traumatised and shut down and had no positive expectations left in his body or soul.

Sadly it has taken months to get Oscar to the point that we can look for a home for him, the damage ran deep. He is still concerned by new people and new situations, but in familiar surroundings with the people he trusts he’s become quite a character. Food has been the key to his heart and he initially learned to love us as life sized good dispensers.

He now appreciates that his humans have more to offer than just food and will allow fuss and affection and even approach to ask for it. He’s still a little wary of the lead going on and off but he enjoys his walks and behaves well.

Oscar will need an experienced adopter and another dog in the home full time is essential. He could live with respectful children aged twelve plus. Adopters will need to expect for him to potentially hide up for the first few days as new situations are still scary.

He has shown that he has the capacity to learn at a steady rate and he wants to be a part of a family and let the last of his walls fall down.

name: Benjamin
description:
Benjamin is a medium sized crossbreed aged 9 to ten years old.

Benjamin was a long term resident at the Botosani public shelter in Romania until we rescued him from there last year. It has taken a while to peel back the layers of damage done by years in that place and only now can we look for his forever home.

Benjamin is a comical old chap with a hint of stubbornness thrown in for comedic effect! He enjoys short walks in decent weather but doesn’t want to go out in the rain Thankyou very much!

He mixes well with other dogs in his foster home but gives the younger generation and their shenanigans a wide berth. Benjamin would like a calm dog in his forever home to show him the ropes.

He isn’t overly affectionate with humans at the moment but in a more one to one environment may become more appreciative of them. I guess he lived without humans for such a long time he learned to live without us…. but that can change with time, love and understanding.

Benjamin would like an adult home environment but visiting children would be fine. He hasn’t met the cat yet but can if needed.

name: Fizz
description:
Fizz is a smallish crossbreed aged around one year old.

We met Fizz on our recent trip to the Botosani public shelter in Romania. She was in pen 104 with three other dogs that were very friendly and good at drawing our attention. It’s really thanks to them that we noticed her as she is not one to push herself forward in a crowd of 800 dogs.

Fizz is a cute but shy little girl who wants to behave like the adolescent she is but until now life had knocked the play out of her. She has been in the UK for a few weeks now and yesterday surprised both us and herself when she picked up a ball. She had no idea what to do with it so just paraded it proudly around her foster siblings.

She is learning to relax and enjoy life but still has a way to go to be completely carefree as she should be. She will need at least one other dog as full time resident in her forever home. She has learnt how to walk on a lead but will need to continue to gain experience in her forever home.

It’s so hard for them when everything around them is new and every experience is a “first”, but this little jewel is so ready to break through her fears niw and just needs somewhere to continue to do so. She can live with children aged ten plus and seems unphased by the cat.

name: Teddy
description:
Teddy is a medium to large crossbreed aged around three to four years old.

Teddy has come into our care recently from Bosnia where he’d resided in a shelter since he was a puppy. He is the first of three siblings to travel to us, the others will travel when his adoption creates a space in foster.

Teddy is such a dignified boy who is loving UK life. Walks are just absolute enlightenment to him and you can just see the joy and wonder in his face as he gets to see life outside of a shelter.

He is a little timid with new people but loves a fuss once he knows you well. He would like the company of another dog in his forever home but would be ok as an only dog if a little extra time was allowed for him to settle.

Teddy is calm and contented around the home and could live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Winnie
description:
Winnie is a small crossbreed aged three to four years old.

Winnie came to us a a couple of years ago from the Radauti public shelter in Romania. She arrived terrified of everyone and everything but over time has emerged into a plucky and cheeky little character who is loved by all in her foster home.

Winnie is still worried by strangers and doesn’t enjoy being picked up but in many ways is a quietly confident little girl who is very popular amongst the pack in her foster home. Winnie will need at least one other steady dog in her forever home. She enjoys her walks but is still a little worried about having her lead put on but this too is improving daily and she is becoming less tense about it.

Winnie has been fine with the safe rescue cat. She would like a settled home environment with no children. Her adopters will need to allow her time to get to know and trust them but she will reward them when she reveals the sweet and clever little character that we have been privileged to uncover.

name: Val
description:
Val is a small to medium sized crossbreed aged four years old.

Val came into our care when she was a puppy, she was soon adopted but has been returned recently because the domestic circumstances had changed.

Val has settled really well back in her foster home. She has been enjoying the company of the other dogs, in particular Tempy who she often initiates play with, we think she would be happiest with another dog for company.

On the first day she was happy to jump up on the sofa next to her foster dad, although initially she wasn’t keen on getting fussed, but already that is changing and especially if food is involved she is happy to have a fuss.

She walks beautifully on a lead and is a pleasure to take out. She is worried by visitors to the home so would like a calm and quiet household.

Val has previously lived happily with cats and could live with respectful children aged twelve plus.

name: Pettern
description:
Pettern is a medium-sized male crossbreed aged 2 year old.

Pettern was abandoned with his siblings outside the gates of the shelter in Crivatu, Romania. Sadly they grew up there whilst waiting for their chance to come to the UK to find a new home.

Pettern is a sweet, affectionate, playful and loyal boy to those he loves. He has been adopted once but as the only dog in the home, he was on edge and anxious so he will need another dog or dogs in his new home. He would need a home with no children.

name: Sallie
description:
Meet Sallie, the sweet little whirlwind with a huge heart.

Sallie – 11 month old female Cross-Breed.

Sallie is currently in foster in Coventry. She is a bright, loving young pup who is looking for a home that can give her the time, routine, and understanding she needs to grow into the wonderful dog she has the potential to be.

She recently flew from Cyprus to her foster home and currently weighs around nineteen kilograms, expected to reach approximately twenty-three to twenty-five kilograms once fully grown.

Sallie is a joyful mix of affection, cheekiness, and curiosity. Once she feels settled and knows her people, she becomes incredibly loving.

She adores cuddling up on the sofa for her quiet moments and is very good at taking herself off to a peaceful corner when she wants a bit of downtime; her crate or the kitchen tub chairs are particular favourites.

• A happy, lively pup who loves to play and explore.• Cheeky, full of life, and wonderfully inquisitive.• Enjoys her independence and will happily potter off for her own space.• Obsessed with stuffed toys—the noisier the better.

Sallie is at that puppy stage where everything is new and exciting, and she’s eager to learn. She watches everything you do, takes direction well, and already knows sit and wait.

She thrives with enrichment like stuffed Kongs, Licki mats, and snuffle mats—these help her self-soothe and learn calm behaviours.

• Lead walking: Good on the lead, though she doesn’t like feeling restricted and may try to chew what’s near her. Road walking is still being introduced as she can be nervous.• Food manners: Excellent with humans—takes treats gently. She is currently fed separately from the resident dog as she settles into household routines.• Other dogs: Friendly but a little overenthusiastic in greetings.• People & children: Not kid-tested. Can be vocal with visitors and needs reassurance and guidance. Would be best suited to older, dog-savvy kids.• Cats/small furries: Not tested, likely too exciting for her at this stage.• Crate: Doing well with crate training.

• A calm, experienced home ready for the excitement and fun of a young pup.• Someone able to offer structure, patience, routine, and ongoing training.• Potentially a calm male dog who would enjoy playing with her or a family able to spend time helping her settle.• A home ready for a puppy.

She is a truly lovely girl who just needs the right environment to blossom. With consistency, reassurance, and understanding, Sallie has all the makings of a loyal, cuddly, playful, and wonderfully spirited companion.

If you think you could be the one to help this sweet pup grow into her best self, Sallie would love to meet you.

Please tell us a little about yourself when contacting us:

Your garden and fencing (height at lowest point)

Ages of children in the home or who visit

How long Sallie may be left alone, and how she’ll fit into your lifestyle

Sallie is spayed, vaccinated, and microchipped. A minimum adoption donation of £300 applies. Adoption is subject to a satisfactory application, home check, neutering agreement at her adopter’s expense when she reaches the appropriate age as agreed with your vet, and agreement to our adoption conditions.

We are committed to the lifelong care of our dogs and will always accept their return when space allows. In situations where space is limited, we will endeavour to rehome the dog directly from its current home.

Under no circumstances may the dog be transferred to another UK rescue organisation.

name: Lucky
description:
Lucky is a 3.5-year-old male Collie Cross. He has a calm, gentle nature that makes him immediately endearing, and his soft temperament shines through in everything he does.

Found abandoned, he is now staying in a private shelter in Romania, hoping for someone who can give him the time and care he truly deserves.

Lucky is a 3.5-year-old male Collie Cross. He’s described as extremely friendly, getting along wonderfully with both dogs and cats, making him a great fit for a multi-pet household.

Although he currently weighs around 25kg, he would ideally be closer to 22kg, and a loving home will help him reach his healthy weight.

Lucky is a 3.5-year-old male Collie Cross. He’s fully prepared for adoption, having been vaccinated, neutered, microchipped, and blood tested.

His rescuers mention how lonely he is in kennels, and how much he would thrive with someone who has plenty of time and affection to offer.

Lucky is a 3.5-year-old male Collie Cross. He would make a fantastic companion thanks to his sweetness and steady temperament.

With rescue back-up, a home check, and an adoption fee that includes transport right to your door, he’s ready and waiting for the chance to start a new chapter with his forever family.

name: Nessa
description:
Nessa is a beautiful 2-year-old Mastiff Cross.

Nessa is currently in our kennels in Wrexham, North Wales.

Nessa is very friendly & affectionate, but can be initially wary when meeting new people. She can easily be won round in no time, with a treat or her favourite toy – a tennis ball!

She is a right water baby and loves to dip her toes into an puddle, stream or river!

Nessa is truly a lovely girl with sooo much potential to be an amazing dog, she’s been living a kennel life since she was 8 months old so really deserves a chance at a forever home where she can really thrive

Nessa is strong on the lead and will certainly need more training in this area, as well as with some basic manners (she will jump up uninvited sometimes).

She does however listen to correction well and is very treat/tennis ball driven, so this will help keep her focus to help when she’s on the lead and other areas of her training

We’ve found Nessa to be hit & miss with other dogs, it’s clear she hasn’t had much socialisation around them, so until this has improved she will do best in a pet free home so the focus can solely be on Nessa and training her up to be the best dog!

She will happily walk alongside another dog and doesn’t react, she just doesn’t want to live with one.

Anyone interested in meeting one of the funniest & quirkiest dogs around please get in touch.

Once we have received your application this will be reviewed by our dog team and if you are a suitable match one of our volunteers will be in touch within 7 days to discuss your application in more detail.

You will then be invited to meet the dog, and we encourage 2-3 meet & greets for you to get to know your chosen dog, we are happy to introduce you to multiple dogs on the day of they are suitable matches.

We do request all household members attend meet & greets including resident dogs.

If successful we will request a home check at this stage along with proof of identification and address. We will require written permission from a landlord for all applicants in rented accommodation.

Please note we require all resident dogs to be neutered and up to date with vaccinations before we will proceed with the adoption.

name: Woody
description:
Woody is a 8 year old male Dalmatian. He’s a large, spot-covered lad who brings a whole lot of love everywhere he goes.

His gentle temperament and sweet nature make him the kind of dog who stands out without even trying.

Woody has a loyal streak and thrives when he’s close to his humans. He’s brilliant with adults and can live with older children, happily soaking up attention and affection. Fully vaccinated and neutered, he’s physically ready for his next chapter.

Woody does have some lead reactivity towards other dogs, but adopters will receive full support and guidance to help him feel more confident.

As he can’t live with cats and must be the only dog, he’ll suit a calm home where he can relax without competition. What he truly wants is a comfy sofa and a family who sees just how special he is.

Woody would bring warmth, steadiness and pure devotion to any home lucky enough to have him. He’s affectionate, kind-hearted and ready for a peaceful life where he can finally unwind and enjoy the comfort he deserves.

name: Chloe
description:
Chloe is a 2 year old female German Shepherd cross.

How two pictures can tell such different stories.One shows a defeated, sick dog—malnourished, lethargic, exhausted from trying to survive with leishmania on the streets.

Clearly dumped by her heartless owners once she started to show some tell-tale signs of the condition.

Chloe has shown incredible resilience, bravery and strength of character to become a strong and healthy girl following treatment, no thanks to the people who were supposed to care about her. You can see the change in her profile pictures—she has life in her eyes again.

Now she is back to her healthy self, we can appreciate just what a supremely special and joyful dog she really is! A little shy at first but quick to warm, she adores people—curious, clever, playful, loving, and hugely affectionate all the time. Even when sick,

Chloe continued to wag her tail for her rescuer daily.

Chloe is a little dominant at times with other dogs. She enjoys the company and attention of similar-sized or larger male dogs—this would be her ideal match in a home. She’d also be a great only dog.

Chloe is very obedient, desperate to learn, and highly trainable—all true to her breed mix. She’s pretty good on leash, but outdoor walking and training will need to continue once Chloe reaches her forever home.

She has medium-level energy. It would be great if Chloe were adopted into an active home that appreciates the outdoors, as she will be at her best learning about and exploring the world.

Her leishmania treatment went very well—she responded extremely positively and is back to good energy levels. She has been transformed into a beautifully stunning girl inside and out.

She requires an inexpensive twice-daily tablet and yearly blood tests to manage and monitor her condition. Her leishmania should not be a barrier to adoption, although we realise it takes an extra-special person to take on dogs with lifelong conditions.

Chloe, like all the others, deserves the opportunity of a loving life in a comfy home away from the kennels of a shelter.

Some dogs show you just how special they are through their rescue journey. Chloe has overcome so much to be restored to her former glory—a dog who truly fought to survive.

Rescue backup: Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-registered charityAdoption and travel fees applyPassport / Fully tested and vaccinated / Neutered

name: Lobo
description:
Lobo is a 3-year-old German Shepherd cross.

Lobo sadly doesn’t have the best chances of finding a loving home.

Dogs like him have the odds stacked against them — larger, German shepherd mixes, with a more dominant nature, a trait often found in bigger breeds.

For dogs like him, it can mean a lifetime in a shelter.

It often doesn’t count that these dogs, including Lobo, have phenomenal strength of character, immense loyalty, and a profound, deep love for their chosen human. Their nature is protective — they love hard.

Lobo is no different. He has all those qualities. Shelter staff report a dog who is initially unsure when meeting people but warms up well. He is very friendly and loving with the shelter team.

Lobo will need to be an only dog. An adult household would be best. No small furries. He will need an adopter experienced with larger breeds and/or German shepherd.

Lobo will need training. He’s a strong boy on the lead, and this needs further work. He doesn’t interact well with other dogs — again, further training required.

He’s part working breed, incredibly bright and active. He’ll need his mind as well as his body exercised. Lobo needs an adopter who wants to commit to him, to harness his qualities to his advantage — an adopter willing to invest.

Lobo will give back love and loyalty tenfold to the person who helps him escape the shelter. Such a large part of his life has been spent behind bars, waiting to be seen, waiting to be noticed.

We hope telling Lobo’s story helps him find that special home now. Big dogs lose out all the time. They spend more time in shelters, languishing in kennels for years.

Lobo is just as worthy as any other dog. He’s never felt comfort in that shelter. He has no idea what it feels like to be truly loved. Like so many other shelter dogs, sadly.

Rescue back-up by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK registered charity.

Adoption fee sponsored / travel fees applyHomecheck requiredNeutered, fully vaccinated and testedHe has his passport and is ready to fly!

Adoption fee sponsoredFoster placement consideredCurrently in Cyprus

name: Tally
description:
Beautiful Tally is a 5 year old female American Bulldog, who experienced untold traumas before arriving in the care of the One Wish Dog Foundation. Tally is currently in foster in Oxfordshire.

Before being found by the dog warden, Tally had been moved from pillar to post, being relentlessly bred from before being left to starve in a filthy drug den.

Riddled with mange and dangerously skinny, Tally’s eyes were almost completely closed up from swelling and she had lost most of her fur from infections. Her back legs were also stiff and sore from emaciation, and being kept in a cage with no freedom and exercise.

If you’re following Tally’s journey on our social media pages, you’ll know that this special girl is now recovering from her traumas in a lovely, cosy home and she has made an incredible transformation thanks to expert medical advice and treatment.

You’ll notice from her photos how much better she is looking and feeling now.

Tally is now vaccinated and once she is fully back to health, she will also be spayed. No more pups for this poor darling, we dread to think how many litters she was forced to have.

What is most amazing about Tally is how, despite everything she has been put through by humans, she refuses to lose faith in us.

She looks to us for safety and comfort, and she is so, so gentle and trusting. She’s quite simply incredible and we’re totally committed to finding her happy ever after.?

We’ll accept nothing short of a 5* home for this exceptional soul. She is able to live with other dogs and children. She has been in contact with cats in foster care but we would prefer for her to go to a cat-free home for safety reasons due to her size.

If you think you might be able to offer our amazing Tally a lifetime of love and all the attention in the world, please do get in touch.

name: Pol
description:
Pol is a 4-year-old male English Setter. He was rescued from the pound after being left there for months with Mascotte following their owner’s passing.

Pol has plenty of energy and loves finally having space to run freely in the shelter’s secure outdoor area.

Pol arrived anxious and full of nervous energy, but he has been settling little by little as he gains confidence.

He’s still on the slim side, so the shelter is helping him put on healthy weight.

Pol is sociable with other dogs and shares his kennel peacefully with Mascotte.

The pair eat side by side without issues and enjoy spending time together in their shared space.

name: Cosmo
description:
Cosmo is a 3-year-old male Cross-Breed. He comes across as upbeat and full of charm, carrying himself with a touch more confidence than his sister Nova.

He already shows the kind of gentle personality that makes people warm up to him fast.

Cosmo is currently staying in a private shelter in Romania, waiting for his chance to make the trip to the UK.

He shares a tight bond with Nova, and the two of them move through life like a little ready-made family.

Anyone thinking about adopting a pair would find these siblings a seriously wholesome match.

Cosmo has a small scar on his nose, but it doesn’t dim his sweetness in the slightest. He’s vaccinated, blood tested, and spayed, making him all set for a smooth transition into a forever home.

Pennypaws Rescue will be there with full rescue backup and support, along with a required video home check to make sure everything’s a good fit.

name: Faith
description:
Faith – 5 year old female Spanish Mastin Cross.

Meet Faith. We rescued her about 1 year ago. She’s a wonderful, loving character who adores small children and being a treasured part of a family.

She’s about 4-5 yrs old, 65 cm floor to shoulder, and 36 kg.

Faith is a wise soul, as well as being fun. We’ve had to keep her quiet for months as she needed surgery on her back leg for a luxating patella. The surgery has been successful, but to enable it to last, she should not do strenuous exercise or rough play.

Faith loves her walks and walks beautifully on a lead, never strong, and gets along with most dogs she meets. She’s good with cats too.

She’s a very easy dog to manage and travels beautifully on the back seat of the car. She loves to be near you when you’re driving.

Faith is currently in foster kennels in West Sussex. She can be adopted anywhere in the UK – we can help to arrange transport to get her to you.

She is vaccinated, blood tested, and will have full rescue backup.

If you think that Faith might be your ideal dog, please get in touch!

name: Dan
description:
Dan is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Dan – a young, medium-sized boy with a tender heart and the courage of a survivor. Just 10 months old, he’s gentle, affectionate, and sensitive — a dog who feels deeply and loves wholeheartedly.

He’s playful and loyal, yet calm and careful, watching the world with kind eyes that seem to ask only for understanding and love.

Rescue StoryDan’s life began in the middle of war. Together with his brother Benny and a few other pups, he was discovered by a kind soldier among the ruins of a bombed-out house — their mother had been killed by shrapnel. The soldier cared for them as best he could, sharing his food and shelter in the trenches.

Desperate for help, he sent out a plea online. And our partner rescue replied. But it was hard to find a transport ready to go over 1000 km to frontline to collect pups. And a brave British volunteer, Brian, stepped in and drove deep into the war zone to bring the puppies to safety.

Dan’s journey from the battlefield to the safety of foster care is nothing short of a miracle — proof that kindness still survives even in the darkest times.

More About DanNow living with a foster family in a quiet countryside home, Dan has learned to trust again. He’s fully housetrained, affectionate, and calm indoors. He loves his walks, enjoys playtime in the garden, and is very social with other dogs.

Though a little wary in new surroundings and with unfamiliar people at first, he warms up quickly when shown kindness. On his own ground, he’s alert, but outside the gate he greets everyone with cheerful curiosity.

He’s a bright boy who loves learning and thrives on positive attention. Active, loyal, and gentle — Dan is the perfect companion for someone who wants a true friend by their side.

Ideal FamilyDan will flourish in a rural or semi-rural home, away from city traffic and loud noises. He needs a garden, regular exercise, and a patient, loving family who will help him continue building confidence.

Another friendly female dog is essential to guide and reassure him, as he’s happiest with canine company. Older children (10+) would suit his calm yet playful temperament.

Dan’s story began in fear, but it can end in love. With his kind heart and loyal nature, he’s ready to give his whole soul to the people who give him a chance. Somewhere out there is a family meant just for him — could it be you?

Health InformationDan is fully healthy. Neutered. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Benny
description:
Benny – The Gentle Hero Who Escaped the Front Line

Benny is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Benny – a 10-month-old medium boy whose story began in the chaos of war but is now filled with hope for a peaceful future.

With his soulful eyes, short tail, and gentle nature, he’s a picture of resilience and quiet strength. Kind, affectionate, and loyal to the core, Benny is ready to leave behind the shadows of his past and step into a life full of warmth, love, and security.

Rescue StoryBenny’s story mirrors that of his brother, Dan — both were born into a war zone. Found in a ruined house near the front line, their mother had tragically been killed by shrapnel. A kind soldier discovered the litter and took them into the trenches, caring for them amid explosions and danger.

As the puppies grew, the soldier knew he couldn’t keep them safe forever. He reached out for help, and a brave volunteer named Brian drove across the country into active conflict to bring the pups to safety.

That was the start of Benny’s second chance at life — a story written by courage and compassion.

More About BennyBenny has been living with a foster family in a peaceful countryside home, surrounded by love and nature. Well, the word “peaceful” doesn’t really describe any place in Ukraine now, as missiles and drones (see video) are reaching everywhere and already became a routine there. He’s housetrained, gentle, and eager to please.

In his familiar environment, he’s confident and affectionate — following his person, snuggling on the sofa (“a true couch bug,” as his foster calls him, when Benny refuses to go out in dark and cold), and showering them with loving devotion.

At first, Benny may be a little cautious when meeting new people or exploring new surroundings, but give him just ten minutes and his loving personality will shine through.

He’s friendly with other dogs and loves playtime, walks, and his beloved toys. Indoors, he’s calm and well-behaved; outdoors, he’s lively, curious, and joyful. He adores human touch and melts when gently stroked.

Ideal FamilyBenny would thrive in a rural or semi-rural home, away from city noise and traffic. He needs space to run, play, and explore, as well as a secure garden to enjoy his freedom safely.

He would do best with another friendly female dog for companionship and guidance. An adult home or family with older, gentle children would suit him well, especially those who appreciate dogs who enjoy both play and peaceful sofa time.

Benny has known fear but never lost his kindness. Now, he’s ready for a home where love is constant, hands are gentle, and life is steady. If you’re looking for a devoted, affectionate companion who will return every ounce of love you give — Benny could be your perfect boy.

Health InformationBenny is fully healthy. Neutered. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Lisa
description:
Lisa – The Joyful Sunshine Girl Who Lights Up Every Room

Lisa is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Lisa – a 7-month-old lower-medium girl bursting with positivity, sparkle, and affection. She is the “sunshine child” of the litter — always cheerful, always ready to greet people, always full of bright, joyful energy.

With her playful heart and loving nature, she is ready to bring laughter and light to her forever family.

HighlightsSIZE: Lower-medium now 47 cm/18 kg /medium-growing (will gain 3-4 cm/kg more)SPAYED: YesCHARACTER: Playful • Happy • Sociable • Brilliantly cleverDOGS: Friendly and playfulCATS: Not testedCHILDREN: Great with older kids 8+

Rescue StoryLisa and her siblings, Lord and Nusha, were discovered abandoned on derelict summer-house grounds when they were tiny puppies. Volunteers rescued them from cold and danger, giving them the safety they desperately needed.

More About LisaLisa is pure sunshine — always happy, always open, always ready to love. She fits into any environment effortlessly and treats every new person like a friend. She absolutely adores toys — so much that even while still a bit sleepy after her spay surgery, she dragged her toy into the recovery basket with her.

She is clever, obedient, affectionate, and wonderfully sociable. She enjoys energetic play outside, but at home she settles beautifully.

Her foster says:“She’s a living spark of joy — so friendly, so clever, so open-hearted. She will suit absolutely any family.”

Ideal FamilyLisa will bloom in an active, loving home that enjoys play, walks, training, and companionship. She would thrive with a friendly resident dog who enjoys fun and games, but could also adapt as the only dog if her people are present, playful, and engaged. Gentle older children would adore her, and she would return that love tenfold.

Lisa is joy in a dog’s body — bright, affectionate, and full of life. A family who welcomes her will gain a daily dose of happiness.

Health InformationLisa is fully healthy. Spayed. Has all core vaccines done and is microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before the trip (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Rapunzel
description:
Rapunzel – A Shy Young Beauty Waiting for Her Fairytale Beginning

Rapunzel is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Rapunzel – a one-year-old lower medium girl with the grace of a young model and the soft, cautious heart of a dog who has seen little kindness in her early life.

Rescue StoryRapunzel’s world was silence, emptiness, and rejection. She wandered between overgrown paths and locked cottages, seeking scraps of kindness but finding none. For many months she lived alone among summer houses, a forgotten soul left behind when people drove away. Locals pushed her off their plots, unwanting and unwelcome, yet she never lost her gentle hope that one day someone kind would stop for her.

When rescuers finally brought her to safety, she stepped into a world she didn’t understand — where voices were soft, beds were warm, and no one chased her away.

More About RapunzelRapunzel lives in-house at her foster home and is fully housetrained. Indoors she is a calm, polite and easy dog — she doesn’t chew, doesn’t bark excessively, sleeps soundly through the night, and keeps her space clean. She finds comfort in having her own cosy corner and familiar toys, which help her feel grounded.

With people, she can be shy at first, especially with new surroundings. But once she realises she is safe, she becomes affectionate, gentle and incredibly sweet. She enjoys curling up close, happily shares the sofa or even the bed, and forms a deep bond with those who treat her kindly.

She is cautious in busy places or around traffic, but walks comfortably and confidently in quieter, familiar areas. Rapunzel needs time, patience and reassurance — and in exchange she gives heart-melting loyalty.

With dogs she can be selective. With smaller dogs she may test boundaries, can be bossy and dominant, while with dogs her size or larger, she becomes soft, submissive and even a little flirtatious. She currently lives with cats and simply ignores them.

Ideal FamilyRapunzel will flourish in a gentle, calm household in a quiet rural or semi-rural area, somewhere far from loud traffic and hectic environments. A home with a grassy secure garden will help her settle and decompress at her own pace. She is well suited to a peaceful family with older, respectful children aged 12+ who understand sensitive dogs. Rapunzel can be the only dog or live alongside a friendly calm dog of similar or larger size who won’t overwhelm her.

She is not suited for city life or very busy surroundings.

Rapunzel is a shy young beauty waiting for the soft, patient home where she can finally bloom. With kindness and time, she will reward her family with quiet affection, deep loyalty, and the joy of watching a once-forgotten dog grow into the loving companion she always wished to be.

Health InformationRapunzel is fully healthy, spayed, vaccinated and microchipped. All dogs are C.Brucella tested before travel (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

RBU, post-adoption support, and 4 weeks free PetPlan insurance provided upon adoption.

name: Nusha
description:
Nusha – The Softest Little Bear With a Tender Heart

Nusha is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven. Available under a foster-to-adopt. Expected arrival: 19 December.

Meet Nusha – a 7-month-old lower-medium girl, the gentlest and calmest of her siblings. With her soft “teddy bear” coat, her sweet eyes, and her quiet, delicate nature, she brings peace and warmth everywhere she goes.

Sensitive, affectionate, and beautifully mild-mannered, Nusha is ready to bloom in a safe, loving home.

HighlightsSIZE: Currently Lower-medium 45 cm/15 kg, still growing (below the knee; will gain little more height/weight)SPAYED: YesCHARACTER: Soft-hearted • Calm • Affectionate • GentleDOGS: Friendly, playful, needs canine companyCATS: Not testedCHILDREN: Good with older, gentle kids 8+

Rescue StoryNusha and her siblings, Lord and Lisa, were found abandoned as tiny puppies on derelict summer-house land — left with no food, no shelter, no human help. Volunteers rescued them and brought them into foster care, where they blossomed into wonderfully social, trusting young dogs.

More About NushaNusha is the calmest of the trio. She can quietly entertain herself, doesn’t bother anyone, and seeks affection with a soft, almost shy tenderness. Her coat is plush and velvety, and she absolutely melts when stroked — she freezes in bliss when touched gently.

She forms deep emotional bonds and struggles being an only dog — she needs a friendly resident dog for companionship and reassurance.

Her foster describes her beautifully:“She’s like a small teddy bear. Quiet, sweet, soft… she just wants love. She is happiest when another friendly dog is near.”
