Blue can be rehomed with mature children who are 14+ years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Blue can be rehomed with another dog, as he has interreacted well with others whilst in our care. Again this would be subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Soul
description:
Soul is looking for a special home where she can begin the next chapter of her life. She has come straight from the racing kennels so has never lived in a home before so will need some training to help her adjust. Soul is a sweet, gentle girl who is happy to be fussed all over. She can be a little timid at first in new environments but soon comes around. Once she is in her new home everything is going to be new to her, so she will need a patient family who understands that she needs time to settle and build her confidence.  Once she is settled she has so much potential to blossom into a wonderful companion.

Soul is looking for a home with children who are 14+ who understand that she will need her own space and time to adjust to being in a home. This will be subject to a successful meet.

Soul is paired with another greyhound currently and has socialised well with other dogs in our care, we believe that she can be rehomed with another dog – Subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Bruce
description:
Meet gorgeous Bruce!  Bruce has had a very difficult start in life.  When he first came into our care, he was in a truly sorry state.  He was extremely thin, and his skin was in a terrible condition.  His body was bald, red and very inflamed, and it was clear that he had not had the care he desperately needed.  After lots of veterinary visits, treatment, time and plenty of TLC, we are so pleased to see the changes in him.  His fur is beginning to grow back, he is gaining weight, and he is slowly starting to feel better in himself.  Bruce is a very frightened and timid boy.  The world is a scary place for him, and he can be extremely nervous and shut down.  He will need someone who understands that building his confidence will not happen overnight.  However, once Bruce learns to trust you, you see a completely different side to him.  He is a very affectionate, playful and loving boy who enjoys being close to the people he feels safe with.  Bruce will need lots of time, patience, understanding and reassurance.  His new adopter must be prepared to give him the space he needs and allow him to progress at his own pace.  This could take some considerable time, and there may be setbacks along the way.  He is looking for an experienced owner who has previous experience with very nervous and fearful dogs and understands the commitment involved in helping a dog like Bruce learn that the world can be a safe place.  Bruce has already come such a long way, and we believe there is a wonderful, affectionate boy waiting to emerge as his confidence grows.  He deserves a quiet, patient and loving home where he can finally feel safe, secure and cherished.  The potential adopter must commit to multiple regular meet and greets for Bruce to get to know then before the adoption can take place.  He will need a private secure garden.

Bruce has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, he can be ok with some and very unsure around others, so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where he can get 100% of the love and attention.

As Bruce is so timid we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Toto
description:
Meet Toto!  Toto (18kg) is looking for a patient and loving home where he can continue to build his confidence. When Toto first arrived with us, he was a very nervous and timid boy.  While he has made good progress, he can still be a little unsure when meeting new people, so he needs an adopter who understands that he will need time, patience and plenty of positive experiences to help him come out of his shell.  Once Toto gets to know you, his lovely personality really starts to shine through.  He is a friendly boy who enjoys spending time with his people, loves playing with his toys and absolutely enjoys going out on long walks exploring.  Toto is a clever boy who already knows his basic commands.  He can spin on command and give both paws, and like many Terriers, he is very happy to show off his tricks where there are tasty treats involved! He was also a very good boy at the vets, which was lovely to see given how nervous he can initially be.  Toto walks well on the lead and would make a wonderful companion for an active home that enjoys getting out and about.  He will need his socialisation to continue in his new home, particularly to help him develop his confidence around people and new experiences.  Toto may look quite small on the pictures but he is 18kg.  Toto is looking for an experienced, patient adopter who will allow him to settle at his own pace and continue working positively on his confidence.  Because of his nervous nature, multiple meet and greets will be required before Toto can be adopted.  This is important to allow him and his new adopter to get to know one another and for Toto to feel comfortable with them.  He will benefit from a private secure garden.

Toto has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could potentially be rehomed with another dog following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered)

As Toto came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him, and as he can be quite nervous we would like any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Peggy
description:
Meet Peggy! Peggy is looking for an active and loving forever home.  When she first meets new people, she can be a little nervous, but once she gets to know you, her affectionate and loving personality really shines through.  She absolutely loves cuddles, belly rubs and spending time with her people.  She is a very energetic, playful and high-energy young dog who will need a home that can keep up with her.  An active home who enjoys plenty of walks, playtime, training and enrichment would be ideal for her. She can get over-excited and does tend to jump up, so she will need continued training and consistent boundaries to help her learn appropriate greetings.  On walks, she can become very excited and spins on the lead, so her new adopter will need to continue working patiently on her lead manners.  With time, consistency and positive training, she has plenty of potential to become a fantastic walking companion.  She will need patience while she builds confidence around new people. She is a young dog with lots of love and enthusiasm to give.  She may need a little time to settle and gain confidence, but once she feels comfortable, she is friendly, affectionate and full of fun.  If you are looking for an energetic young companion and are prepared to put the time into training she could be the perfect dog for you. Peggy will need a private secure garden.

Peggy has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel she could potentially be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered)

As Peggy came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she can be a little nervous around new people we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Mischief
description:
Meet Mischief!  This lovely girl is looking for a very special home.  Mischief is a very timid and nervous girl who has slowly started to come out of her shell.  She will need patient, understanding adopters who are willing to give her the time and space she needs to build confidence and learn that she is safe.  Once Mischief trusts you, you get to see the sweet girl underneath.  She is affectionate and loving, enjoys giving kisses, and absolutely loves a good belly rub.  Seeing her begin to relax and show her gentle personality is incredibly rewarding.  Mischief does have a cheeky side to her name!  She is a talented escape artist and has been known to jump the kennel walls, so her new home will need secure fencing and adopters who are prepared for her Houdini tendencies.  Extra care will be needed to make sure the doesn’t escape open doors or fences.  Mischief is not looking for a busy or rushed home.  She needs someone who understands that trust takes time and is willing to let her progress at her own pace.  Any potential adopters will need to commit to several regular meet and greets before the adoption can take place.

Mischief has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, although she does prefer a calmer dog.  We do feel she could be rehomed with another calm dog following a successful meet and greet (must be neutered).

As Mischief came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she can be very nervous we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Baloo
description:
Baloo came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information about him. From day one he has been super friendly and loveable towards everyone he meets. He always jumps up for kisses and cuddles! He is a big dopey boy that is after a family that can provide him with all of the love that he deserves. He enjoys playing with his toys and going for little walks around the woods. He can be strong on his lead at times due to excitement. Once out and about he enjoys a relaxing stroll taking in all of the different smells. He is looking for a home that is more relaxed as he isn’t a dog that needs a lot of walking, but plenty of cuddles is needed!

Baloo can be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Baloo could potentially be rehomed with another dog that is also quite calm – Subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Marley
description:
Meet Marley!  Marley is a very lively and energetic boy with plenty of personality!  He absolutely loves to play and, if you let him, would happily spend all day playing fetch.  He is looking for a home that can keep up with his energy levels and provide him with plenty of exercise, playtime, enrichment and attention.  Marley is very unsure of new people so will need time for him to gain his trust.  Marley is a very vocal character.  He certainly knows how to let you know when he wants your attention and isn’t afraid to speak up!  His cheeky personality and enthusiasm make him a fun and engaging companion for the right person.  When Marley first arrived with us, he found having his lead put on very difficult and would react towards the staff.  As Marley came into our care as a stray, we have no history for him, so unfortunately we don’t know what may have happened in his past or why he is so worried about his lead.  Our staff have been patiently working with Marley to help him feel more comfortable, and we are pleased to say that he is making great progress and is getting better.  His new adopter will need to continue this work at his pace, using patience, consistency and positive experiences to help build his confidence.  Marley is looking for a very active home that understands he will need ongoing training, patience and plenty of physical and mental stimulation.  In return, he has the potential to be a wonderful, fun-loving companion who will keep you entertained with his playful nature and big personality.  He will need a private secure garden as he can be a bit of an escape artist.  Marley is not the dog for a first time dog owner.

Marley has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care and is very unsure around them and can be vocal, so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where his new adopter can carry on his training and socialisation around other dogs using lots of positive reinforcement.

name: Chance
description:
Meet Chance!  He is a lovely, friendly boy who absolutely adores people and loves nothing more than lots of fuss, attention and affection.  He is a real character and will happily make sure you know when he wants attention!  Chance can be quite an excitable boy and will jump up when seeking attention.  When he becomes over-stimulated, he can also be a little humpy so his new adopter will need to be prepared to calmy redirect him and help him learn appropriate ways to manage his excitement.  He can be vocal in kennels and is also a bit of an escape artist, so secure surroundings and a family who can keep a close eye on him will be important.  The good news is that Chance has already had his BOAS surgery and has made a full recovery.  His health and breathing have been carefully supported, and he is now fully recovered from the procedure.  Chance is a fun, affectionate and loving little boy with plenty of personality.  He is looking for a home that will give him the time, patience and structure he will need.  He will also need a private secure garden.

Chance has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care but can be a little ‘humpy’ with them so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where his adopter can work on his manners when interacting with other dogs.

As Chance came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Shep
description:
Shep is an older boy who is looking for a calm retirement home. Shep is an affectionate boy who roles over for belly rubs and paws at you for attention. He does have unusual eyes but that just adds to his charm. Shep needs a home with a family that has previous experience with herding breeds.

Shep needs an adult only home so that he can spend his golden years relaxing in a calm environment.

Shep can be a little unsure around certain dogs, usually big and boisterous dogs, but can interact well with smaller calm dogs. Due to this we feel that it would be best for Shep to be the only dog in the home. Shep would benefit from socialisation training to help his confidence.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Bear
description:
Bear is a very nervous boy when he meets new people for the first time. It takes a little while for him to come around but with patience and yummy treats he slowly starts to trust you. Once he has gained your trust and is comfortable he is an affectionate boy and loves to give out kisses. He will need to have multiple regular meets before going home.

Bear is a big dog who doesn’t understand his size, he is constantly jumping up for cuddles and doesn’t know what personal space is. Bear is going to require a lot of training to help him learn manners. He can be a very cheeky boy at times! He will need socialising in different environments and around people to help him build his confidence up. Bear gets super excited when going for walks and is very strong on the lead, this is another area that will need more training. Bear loves playing with his toys, splashing around in water and zooming around our enclosed area.

Bear is after an adult only home that has previous experience with big boisterous dogs. No regular visiting children either please. He is going to need a very active home with a family that is able to provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to keep him busy. As he is still only a young dog he can get up to mischief when he is bored. Bear’s new family need to be committed to putting in the training that he needs not only initially but keeping it up for the rest of his life.

Bear needs to be the only dog in the home so that he can have all of attention to help get him settled. Bear can interact well with dogs whilst out on walks but will need further training to help improve this.

We know that Bear is going to require a lot of work at first but once he is trained he will make a lovely family dog who will love going on plenty of adventures. Taking on a dog this size is a big commitment, please ensure that you are serious and have thought about the future before applying.

name: Freddie
description:
Despite his age Freddie is still full of life and ready to go on lots of adventures with his new family. He loves being out and about exploring and having plenty of sniffs. Once he’s been out for a walk and had a play he is more than happy to curl up in his bed, or preferably your lap and snooze the afternoon away. He is a very loveable and cuddly dog so needs a family that can spoil him and provide him a loving home he deserves.

Freddie needs to be in an adult only home so that he can have his own space to relax.

Freddie is a typical little dog and doesn’t like dogs being in his personal space, he needs to be the only dog in the house. He would benefit from further socialisation around dogs.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Heidi
description:
Heidi is a sweet girl who loves attention and a cuddle! She is very much a typical spaniel, full of energy and always ready for an adventure! She is going to need a very active home that has a lot of extra time to put in the training that she needs to become a well mannered girl. Heidi is still a young dog so can be very cheeky at times. Her new family will need to have Spaniel experience as the  behaviours she has been showing are typical to the breed. Heidi will need a lot of exercise and mental stimulation every day to keep her mind and body active and to prevent her from causing mischief. Heidi is going to require a lot of hard work to train her to become a great family dog but with time, patient and a lot of energy we believe that she will get there.

Heidi needs to be in an adult only home with no regular visiting children.

Heidi is a friendly girl and loves to meet dogs out and about on walks but we believe that she needs to be the only dog in the home so that her new family can focus on her training and she can get all of the attention she needs.

If you think that you can provide a patient and loving home for Heidi please apply today!

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Gordon
description:
This handsome boy is Gordon!  He is looking for a loving, quiet home to enjoy his retirement.  Gordon can be a little nervous when he first meets you, but give him a little time and patience and you’ll soon see his sweet personality shine through.  Once he’s settled, he is a friendly, affectionate and lovely boy.  One thing Gordon certainly isn’t shy about is letting you know what he thinks!  In his kennel, he is very vocal and is the loudest boy on the block and definitely has plenty to say.  Once away from the kennel environment, he is much happier and can relax and show you what a sweet boy he really is.  Gordon is also a big fan of his food – winning his heart may well be as simple as offering him a tasty treat!  At 10 years old. Gordon is looking for a quiet retirement home where he can take life at a slower pace, feel safe and secure, and be surrounded by people who will give him the love he deserves.  If you’re looking for a sweet older gentleman with a big voice, an even bigger appetite and a lovely personality waiting to come out, Gordon could be the boy for you.

Gordon has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel following a successful meet and greet, he could potentially live with another small dog.

As Gordon came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Tuco
description:
This handsome boy is Tuco! (21kg)  He has a big personality and an even bigger zest for life!  This friendly lad loves meeting people and is always ready for his next adventure.  Tuco is full of energy and would thrive in an active family who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks, and exciting days out exploring.  Whether it’s hiking, woodland walks, or trips to the beach, Tuco will be your enthusiastic companion every step of the way.  In kennels, Tuco can be very vocal and loud, but this is just his way of expressing himself.  Once he’s out and spending time with people, his affectionate and loving nature really shines through.  As a young, energetic dog, Tuco still has a few manners to learn.  He can be quite strong on the lead and would benefit from continued training to improve his lead walking and learn some basic commands.  He can also be a little humpy when he’s over-excited, so his new adopter will need to be patient and consistent in helping him channel his enthusiasm in more appropriate ways.  Grooming isn’t Tuco’s favourite pastime, and he’s not particularly keen on being brushed, so this is something his new owner will need to work on gradually using positive reinforcement.  Tuco is a lovely boy with so much potential.  With the right active home, ongoing training, and plenty of love, he’s sure to grow into an amazing companion.  If you are looking for a fun-loving, energetic best friend to share life’s adventures with, Tuco could be the boy for you.  He will need a private secure garden.

Tuco has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, he can be a little unsure at first and does prefer a calmer female.  We do feel he could potentially be rehomed with another dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Tuco came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ell
description:
Meet Ell!  She is looking for a loving home where she can continue to build her confidence.  When you first meet Ell, she can be very nervous and timid.  New people and unfamiliar situations can be overwhelming for her, but once she knows and trusts you, her sweet personality begins to shine.  She simply needs an experienced, patient owner who will give her time and space to settle at her own pace.  Once she’s comfortable, Ell is incredibly friendly and affectionate.  She loves belly rubs and enjoys lots of fuss.  She’s not particularly interested in toys, but she does love exploring the world and having a good sniff on walks.  In kennels, Ell can be very vocal, so she will need understanding neighbours and owners who appreciate that she may bark at first but this is just her way of expressing herself.  She can sometimes be a bit growly when she’s at the vets, but this is fear-related, and she benefits from calm, gentle handling during stressful situations.  Ell is currently carrying a little extra weight, so her new adopter will need to help her on a healthy weight-loss journey with sensible exercise and a balanced diet.  This will help improve her overall health and wellbeing.  Ell is looking for a kind, patient home that will see past her initial nerves and give her the chance to blossom. She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Ell has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel she could live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ell came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her and as she can be a little nervous we would like any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Morgan
description:
Morgan came into our care through no fault of his own. Due to him being a rehome we do have some knowledge of what he was like in the home and he is already toilet trained. Morgan is a very friendly boy and loves to say hello to everyone he meets. Morgan spends most of his day relaxing on his comfy bed surrounded by his fluffy toys, which he likes to show off. Morgan is currently on a weight loss journey and will need to continue this when he goes home. Morgan is after a loving retirement home where he can spend his days lounging on his own comfy sofa. Morgan loves to go out for little walks and lots of sniffs!

Morgan can be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Morgan needs to be the only dog in the house as he is after a peaceful and calm retirement home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Bob
description:
Bob is a sweet boy but can be nervous of new people, especially around men. Bob is currently under training to help to reduce his nervousness around men and new people, his new family will need to be patient and may need to have extra meets to ensure that he is familiar of everyone in the house before he goes home. Bob will need continuous training to help with his socialisation skills. Once bob is comfortable his goofy personality soon comes out, he loves to play with his toys and all of the staff here. Bob loves his walks, due to his size he can be strong on the lead but with a little more training that would improve. Bob loves his treats and enrichment activities in between walks. Bob is a clever boy as he already knows a few tricks such as sit, down and paw.

Bob needs an adult only home where he can have plenty of space to settle in and gain more confidence. He will need an experienced home that has had large breed dogs before and can handle his size and boisterous behaviour once he is settled.

Bob has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, he is still only young so he does like to bounce around and try and play with dogs. Further training is needed to help him improve his manners. Bob could potentially be rehomed with another dog – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Arlo
description:
Meet Arlo! Arlo is a gorgeous, sweet-natured boy who is very friendly and absolutely loves lots of fuss.  He’s a real people dog and enjoys getting plenty of attention and affection.  He is a very energetic and boisterous lad who can get extremely giddy when he’s excited.  He sometimes forgets just how big he is and will jump up to say hello, so he would benefit from some basic training to help him learn his manners and channel all that enthusiasm.  Arlo recently had a bath, and although he was a little nervous to begin with, he was a very good boy.  Once it was all over, he celebrated in true Arlo style with a case of the zoomies!  He also has a funny habit of rearranging his bed and moving it to wherever he thinks it should be.  Arlo is a loveable, fun, lively character with bags of personality.  He would thrive in a very active home with someone who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks and consistency with his training.  He would need a private secure garden so he can practice his zoomies!

Arlo has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful, so we feel following a successful meet and greet he could live with another dog of similar size and energy level.

As Arlo came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Star
description:
Star can be a little shy and quiet at first whilst she gets to know you but does like a fuss. As she has come out of her shell more, she can get giddy and excited. She loves her walks and can pull when she is interested in a certain smell. As she gets more confident and settles we do believe her cheeky terrier side will come out. She certainly has plenty of energy! We have learnt that Star doesn’t like to be left and does struggle with this. We are looking for a home who are willing to continue working with Star on this, with time and patients to do so.

Due to her still being a little nervous Star may require multiple meets so she can get to know her new family before going home. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding whilst she is settling in and getting used to her new surroundings.

We think that it is best for Star to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Star has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so can potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar temperament – subject to a successful meet.

We wouldn’t recommend Star to be rehomed with cats due to her breed.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Nibbles
description:
Nibbles is a young boy who is full of energy and has a lot of love to give. Nibbles loves being off lead in our enclosed area running around chasing tennis balls. He has a lot of energy so will need a very active home with a family who can take him out on lots of adventures to burn off his energy. He would benefit from mental stimulation in between walks to keep his brain stimulated. Due to being a young dog Nibbles will need further training to help him grow up to be a well mannered boy, he can be a little nippy at times too.

Nibbles came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any history on him. Due to being very friendly we think that he can be rehomed with dog savvy children who are 16 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Nibbles is friendly with every dog he meets and always wants to play. He can potentially be rehomed with another dog that can tolerate his high energy and playfulness – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Kong
description:
Kong is a loveable and friendly giant who is always happy,  and maybe a little too enthusiastic, to say hello to everyone he meets. Kong is still only a young boy so doesn’t know his strength and size. Further training will need to be done to ensure he can be taught manners. Kong does currently like to jump up so a family with experience around large breeds would be beneficial. Kong is a sweet boy and always greets staff in the morning with a blanket in his mouth and a very waggy tail!

Kong came into our care as a stray from another kennels so we don’t have any history on him or know if he has lived in a home before. Due to this and his size, Kong is best to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Kong has interacted well with friendly dogs whilst in our care but can be very boisterous and over the top. He will need continuous socialisation to help train him to react appropriately around dogs. He could potentially be rehomed with another dog that has a calm and friendly temperament but it is preferred for him to be the only dog in the home so that he can get all of the attention to help with his training. This would be subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Ziggy + Frankie
description:
Ziggy and Frankie came into our care due to no fault of their own. They are both sweet boys who love cuddles and attention but have to gain your trust first. Frankie is more confident around people than Ziggy is, so multiple meets may be needed before they can go home. Due to them both still being young dogs they will need continued training to help them grow into well behaved pooches. As with most Dachshunds they both do like to talk a lot in the kennels and out of walks, this is something to take into consideration if you want a quiet life. Ziggy loves to go for walks and to sprint around whilst offlead in an enclosed area. Frankie on the other hand does prefer to be picked up and carried around and isn’t a fan of the lead or the outdoors. He will need more training with his new family so that he can build his confidence and learn what his little legs are for. Off lead in an enclosed area he does join in running around with Ziggy and they both do love playing and wrestling together. The pair have been together since they were young puppies so are well adjusted to living together, they even enjoy sharing their food at meal times. They cannot be rehomed separately.

Due to their ages they can be a little cheeky at times so we are looking for their new family to have plenty of time to put into their training and socialisation. We would recommend that they are taken to classes to help support you with this. They are going to need patience whilst they adjust to their new living arrangements as they have had a lot of new changes recently at such a young age. We need their new family to be serious about taking the pair with on as they are ready to find their forever home!

We believe that Ziggy and Frankie can be rehomed with dog savvy children over the age of 12 years. Due to their barking and nerves at first all children must be confident around dogs. They have previously lived with children. This is subject to a successful meet.

We believe that Ziggy and Frankie should be the only dogs in the home. This is due to them requiring more socialisation when first meeting dogs. They can both say hello to other dogs, after they have done a lot of shouting first, but do need to build their confidence, especially Ziggy.

They are both very cute and are going to be popular. Please consider all of your circumstances and any changes that could happen that would affect the boys in the future before applying. They are not currently available to view at the centre.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias needs a little more training around dogs since his castration as he has become a little unsure, therefore we believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Dakota
description:
Dakota is looking for her forever home, and she has so much love to give.  She’s an incredibly sweet, friendly girl who absolutely adores people.  If you’re happy to give her plenty of fuss, she’ll be in her element!  Despite her size, she is a gentle soul with a lovely nature and enjoys spending time with her favourite humans.  She already knows some basic commands and is very eager to please so would benefit from further training.  Being a young, strong dog, she can be powerful on the lead, so her new adopter will need to be confident and committed to continue her lead training.  Because of this, she will be best suited to an active home where she can enjoy plenty of exercise, adventures and mental stimulation.  If you are looking for a loyal, affectionate companion with a heart as big as she is, this lovely girl could be the one for you.  She will need a private secure garden.

She has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, and is very playful and can be too much for other dogs as she does get in their face so for this reason we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can continue to learn manners and boundaries around other dogs will the full support of her new adopter with lots of positive reinforcement.

As Dakota came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Jax
description:
This stunning boy is Jax! we are looking for an experienced home for this fantastic lad.  He is a friendly and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and enjoys a good fuss.  He has a wonderful nature and is always happy to spend time with his people. This clever lad is exceptionally well behaved at the vets, taking examinations and handling in his stride, which is a testament to his temperament and trainability.  Like many dogs, he has his own little quirks – one of his favourites is enthusiastically ragging his blankets and rearranging them to his liking!  As a typical Belgian Malinois, he is highly intelligent, energetic and thrives on both physical exercise and mental stimulation.  He loves charging around our compound and would be happiest in a home where he has plenty of opportunities to stay active and engaged.  Because of his breed traits, he will need an owner who has previous experience with Belgian Malinois and understands their needs.  He is not a dog that will be content with a short walk around the block, he requires ongoing training, enrichment and a lifestyle that allows him to use both his body and brain.  He will need a private secure garden.

Jax was rehomed but sadly has been returned to us as his prey drive was too much for his new owners. He cannot be rehomed with cats or small furries.  He will need an owner that has previous experience with large breed high prey dogs.

He has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could possibly be rehomed with another dog (similar size) following a successful meet and greet.

As Jax came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Daisy
description:
Daisy was previously a racing greyhound who has been brought up in kennels. She is a smaller girl in comparison to a typical greyhound but still does have quite a high prey drive. She makes up for her size with her big personality, she is a very sweet and loving girl but can be a little cheeky at times. As like most greyhounds, Daisy enjoys a good walk and sniff in the woods, with the occasional time off lead in an enclosed area to burn off energy but will equally spend lots time relaxing on a comfy cosy bed. Daisy is after someone that is looking to give a dog lots of love and companionship, which she hasn’t previously had in her life. She in return will give you unconditional love.

Daisy can be a little nippy at times so we feel that it would be best for her to be rehomed with children who are 14 years or older – subject to a successful meet.

Daisy is currently paired and used to living with another greyhound in kennels. She has also interacted well with other dogs whilst on walks so we believe that she could be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and temperament – again subject to a successful meet.

Due to Daisy being an ex-racer it wouldn’t be suitable for him to be rehomed with cats or small furries.

name: Ivan
description:
This handsome lad is Ivan!  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a big personality and an even bigger heart.  Full of energy and enthusiasm, he’s always ready for fun and loves nothing more than chasing after tennis balls.  He’s a very excitable and giddy dog who doesn’t always realise his own size, so he can jump up when greeting people or when he’s excited.  He is also quite vocal at times, especially when he wants your attention.   He knows his basic commands and is eager to interact with people, but he will need continued training and guidance, particularly when out walking as he is very strong on the lead.  Due to his size and strength, he would benefit from an experienced and active owner who can continue his training and provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation.  Ivan would benefit from a private secure garden where he can safely have off lead time to play fetch with his tennis balls.

Ivan has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he potentially could be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Ivan came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Buddy
description:
This loveable boy is Buddy! He is the perfect mix of playful energy and affectionate companionship. He’s a friendly, easy-going lad who absolutely adores people and loves being the centre of attention.  Full of character, he’s excitable, giddy and always ready to make you smile.  Whether it’s cuddles on the sofa or a game in the garden, he just wants to be involved in everything you do.  He is bursting with energy and would thrive in an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, playtime and mental stimulation.  Fetch is one of his favourite games, and he will happily keep you entertained for hours chasing after a ball.  Buddy is incredibly affectionate and loves a fuss, he will make a loyal, loving companion.  One thing to note : He is quite the escape artist, so he will need a private secure garden and owners who are mindful of doors, gates and fencing.  When Buddy came into us he had an Entropian (an eye condition) which has now been repaired and he is healing nicely.

Buddy has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he could potentially live with another high energy dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Buddy came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Mercy
description:
Mercy came into our care as a stray, very shut down and scared. With time and patience staff managed to win her round and she slowly came out of her shell. Little by little we are seeing her lovely personality shine through. With those she trusts, Mercy has shown to be very affectionate and sweet lady.

She is still a little unsure, especially around men. However, this is something we are currently helping her with, and her new family must be willing to continue this.

With Mercy being nervous and unsure she is looking for a very patient and understanding adult only home, where she can develop and settle in at her own pace. Her new family must have the time to be able to come and meet her multiple times so she can get to know you before she goes home.

Mercy is currently also having socialisation training around dogs to build up her confidence. She is still unsure of other dogs so needs to be the only dog in the home.

name: Ronnie
description:
Ronnie is a friendly girl who is looking for a caring forever home. She is a bouncy girl that is full of energy and would love to go for lots of adventures. She constantly wants to be out on walks and tries her hardest to escape from the kennel when the door is open- she’s a cheeky monkey! She is super friendly with everyone she meets and enjoys shouting at you if you try to ignore her- she constantly wants attention. She’s a good girl who is happy and can settle down once she’s had a walk and her breakfast, if its something yummy as she is quite fussy. She loves to snuggle up in bed and snooze in the afternoon.

Ronnie has socialised well with dogs she has met in our care so we believe that she can be rehomed with another dog – subject to a successful meet. She is a friendly girl but can get a little jealous when the attention isn’t on her, so we believe it would be best for her to be rehomed with children 12+ and who are confident around dogs.

name: Nova
description:
Nova is a very sweet friendly girl, who enjoys having a good cuddle and fusses with staff and volunteers here at the home. She is absolutely food obsessed, so if you’ve got food, she’ll be your best friend. At times she can get a little over excited with food. Nova would be best suited to a home with knowledge of her breed and have previously owned a dog before. She can also at times be a little strong on her lead, so her new home must be willing to continue to help with training.

With Nova coming into our care as a stray, we don’t have any previous history on her. We think Nova would be best suited to a home with children no younger than 14 years old – subject to a successful meet.

During her time with us, Nova has been sociable towards other dogs but does prefer her own space and at times been typical of the breed, liking the sound of her own voice. For this reason, we believe she would be better as only dog in the home.

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, she came in as a stray so we don’t know much about her history. It has taken a lot of time and patience for Cali to show us her excitable, bubbly personality. Due to this we are after an experienced home that has the time to get to know Cali here before she goes home. Once Cali gets to know you she loves a fuss and attention.  She loves going out for woodland walks and gets very giddy for her lead, she pulls a little on the lead, due to her size, so would benefit from some on going training. Cali enjoys an offlead run in the enclosed compound where she can chase after a tennis ball.

Cali will need to live in an Adult only home with an enclosed garden where she has space to roam about at her leisure.  She used to be a little nervous and unsure around certain dogs, we have been working with her on this and introducing her to dogs which is helping her social interactions. She is now a friendly girl with most of the dogs on site and can say a lovely face to face hello and even tries to play with others. She will need continued training to help with her socialisation. We still feel that Cali will need to be the only dog in the house.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Arlo
description:
Arlo is a very giddy boy who will always bring you a toy when you greet him and just wants to play! He is super friendly and loves everyone that he meets! He is always wagging his tail and wiggling his body when you go to say hello! He loves to explore the woodland area on his walks and will sniff everything along the way. He also adores going into the secure compound area where he can be let off the lead and have as many zoomies as he wants! Arlo will need an active family that is happy to be outside with him a lot.

Arlo can be very vocal when he sees other dogs, but he is capable of interacting well with calm, friendly dogs when introductions are managed appropriately. He would benefit from continued socialisation and training to help him develop better manners and build his confidence around other dogs. Arlo can be powerful on the lead and will pull enthusiastically towards other dogs, so he is looking for a confident owner who is comfortable handling large, strong dogs and is committed to continuing his training. Due to this Arlo needs to be the only dog in the home.

Arlo needs to be in an adult only home with no regular visiting children.

Arlo would benefit from a house with a very secure large garden in a quiet area that doesn’t have much footfall going past as he gets easily overwhelmed with noises. Arlo is a sweet young dog looking for a patient and loving home where he can continue to learn and thrive. With consistent training, guidance, and plenty of opportunities to channel his natural instincts in positive, appropriate ways, he’s sure to grow into a wonderful companion.

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Flash
description:
I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed. Since then, we’ve watched him grow from a worried boy into a much more confident and affectionate companion, and he continues to make us proud every single day.

Flash is still very much a character, goofy, playful, and full of energy but beneath his bouncy exterior lies a gentle heart that just wants to love and be loved. He can be sensitive in new situations and still finds the world a little overwhelming at times, but with people he trusts, his sweet and loyal nature shines through. Once Flash bonds with you, he is yours for life.

Recently, he’s been showing us more of his loving side. On rainy days when we huddle together out of the downpour, he rolls over for belly rubs, brings his toys for attention, and happily drifts off to sleep during a cuddle. It’s in these quiet moments that his true personality comes out, affectionate, trusting, and eager to please.

Flash’s training is going from strength to strength. He’s mastered “touch” (booping his nose to your hand) and is now learning “place.” He still gets a little mouthy when he’s overexcited, but he’s come a long way since his arrival and continues to improve with patience and consistency. He’ll need his future family to have ex-breeding experience and to continue this gentle guidance in the home so he can keep building on all the progress he’s made.

Being an active breed, Flash loves his walks and enjoys exploring the world at his own pace. He’s happiest in calm, quiet areas where he can relax and take everything in without feeling rushed. He will need to be the only pet in the home, as he prefers human companionship over other animals, and he’s not a fan of pigeons or seagulls either!

Flash has had successful surgery for entropion in both eyes, he received care for mild dermatitis around both eyes, but this has since cleared. He is currently being treated for sore and sensitive ears.

What Flash truly needs now is a calm, understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeding experience and with someone who’s around most of the time, someone who can offer him patience, structure, and all the love he deserves. With time and trust, Flash will repay his person a hundred times over with loyalty, affection, and that special spark that makes him so unforgettable.

Please don’t overlook this beautiful boy. Flash has come so far and is ready to start the next chapter of his life he’s just waiting for that one person to believe in him and bring him home.

Flash will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Flash recently spent 3 nights in a home environment & did INCREDIBLY well!He got along brilliantly with our 11-year-old female dog and was very respectful around our two cats. After  initial excitement, he simply wanted to have a sniff, say hello and then settled around them really nicely.Flash absolutely loved being out on his walks. He passed other dogs calmly and only showed a little excitable frustration around a puppy because he just wanted to play!His lead manners were also great, walking nicely to heel for most of the walk. The only time he got a little eager and pulled was when he realised we were heading towards the beach — which quickly became one of his favourite places!We also took him to a secure field where he had a brilliant time running around freely with our resident dog, where we practiced some recall which looked promising!Back at home, Flash was calm, affectionate and loved nothing more than a cuddle on the sofa, with the occasional cue to play with our dog.He was 100% clean in the house without a single accident too!Although Flash can appear reactive in the rescue environment, his time in a home showed a very different side to him. He was calm, well-behaved, super affectionate and a pleasure to have around.These three nights gave us a lovely glimpse of the dog he could be, once settled into the right home

Flash has officially been waiting for a home for a whole year. After a first few months of (a lot of) patience and training, it's then blossomed into the most incredible remaining months where we’ve really seen Flash’s true heart and soul. This dog is phenomenal in more ways than one, and it’s so sad he’s now become part of the MT furniture, and that the rescue has now become his home.

So for Flash’s 1 year anniversary, I took him off site to the nearby country park for a lovely stroll, followed by a visit to McD’s for some chicken nuggets.

Flash was suuuuuuch a good boy on his walk. He took in all the new smells, and took the new environment in his stride. He was even approached by 3 off lead small dogs, and didn’t react at all. He trotted along the park, with the world at his feet and it was the most amazing thing to see.

He is an absolute darling in the car, so we made a swift visit to McD’s for a box of 20 nuggets to eat together in our on site flat.

It was so nice to see Flash in a home like environment, he jumped straight on the sofa, and wandered around inspecting every room. We sat on the floor together eating our nuggets, and he eventually rested on the raised bed and had a little snooze.

It was heartbreaking putting him back in his kennel, when he seemed so at peace and settled in the flat. I just wish there was someone out there who could see him for everything he is and more!!!

Our beautiful, bonkers Flash has learnt a new trick and we thought we would share.

Flash has also been enjoying the sunshine with lots of walks and plays in the yards this week.

Flash continues to work hard on growing his calmness around new people and he is doing ok. He has now been 10 months here at the rescue and has an increasing fan base amongst the staff but he of course longs for a home and people of his own.

When I first started working with him, I was apprehensive. He was a much larger dog than I was used to working with, and he would mouth you til his hearts content. Not because he is a nasty dog, or means any harm whatsoever, but simply because he has come from a home (just out of puppyhood) and he has become extremely anxious and unsettled being in a kennel environment. On top of that, he has been taught 0 manners which definitely didn’t help with the matter!!! I struggled to bond with him, I struggled to understand why he wouldn’t listen when being told, and why all he wanted to do was treat my arm like a toy…

However I found myself thinking, what has Flash been through in his life that was ever HIS fault? He didn’t ask to spend so much of his life in kennels. He never asked to be put in situations where his anxiety gets the better of him, it was never his decision to not be trained to behave normally. So I decided to buck up my ideas and realise he’s not as scary as he seems, and he’s probably just as anxious being around me as I was him. And from that moment on, our relationship has blossomed…

This boy is truly a superstar in every sense of the word. He is SUCH a goofball, and can have you in fits of laughter within seconds of being with him. His personality is infectious, and as soon as he is comfortable with you and realises you are no threat to him, he shines like the star he is. It’s gutting that Flash doesn’t allow every staff member to see all sides of him. The side that shows his softness, his sweetness, his kindness. But that just makes me so much more grateful that he feels comfortable enough around me to do so.

You can see from his pictures, Flash is muzzle trained. Not because he is an aggressive dog, not because he is a violent dog, it’s simply due to his anxiousness. On one hand, Flash is a super intelligent Poodle but on the other hand, he doesn’t really show it. His anxiety gets the better of him, and he puts himself in uncomfortable positions with new people & then panics whilst he’s in it. It is SUPER important that whoever adopts Flash’s main priority is keeping him safe, and keeping him from making decisions that he feels uncertain about. He wants to make friends with everyone, but also decides halfway through some interactions that he’s not to keen on the thought too!

Among (of course) all of the other precious angels I look after the rescue, Flash is one of the reasons I get excited to go to work. You shouldn’t really have favourites, but Flash does take the cake. I cherish every single moment I get with him. Our lovely strolls up the country lanes, our snuggles in the back of his kennel after a long day, our zoomies down our big play yard. Every single moment & memory I look forward to recreating every single day. Nothing tops being around this dog, nothing else matters when you’re with Flash.

If I was in a position to take him home & work with him through his quirks, I absolutely would, in heartbeat in fact. There is just something so special about him, and I truly envy whoever is fortunate to adopt this incredible young man. And for as long as Flash remains in kennels, I will advocate for him, make him feel safe, comfortable and most of all loved.

Flash has completely changed my mind about Poodles. I am absolutely in love with him. He might not be the sharpest boy in the bunch, but he more than makes up for it with his goofy charm and endless silliness.We are still working on his mouthing when he becomes overexcited. Progress is steady, and every small step forward feels like a real achievement. Flash loves his freedom. We take daily trips to the big yard where he runs around like the happiest whirlwind you have ever seen. He would really benefit from visits to private dog fields where he can safely zoom and explore to his heart’s content.Meeting new people can still be a little tricky for him, but we have a careful plan in place to help him do so safely and comfortably. For those of us who know Flash well, he shows a side many would not expect. Beneath his anxiousness and the need for a muzzle at times is the sweetest, softest boy who adores snuggles and head tickles.He loves to stay close, gently resting his head in your lap until he drifts off to sleep. At the end of each day, we share a quiet moment together, curled up side by side until his eyes close and he is peacefully dreaming.Flash truly is a special boy who deserves a very special home. He needs someone who can offer love, patience, and understanding. In return, he will give unwavering loyalty and companionship for life.

Flash is an absolute character, this boy is full of life and once he knows you he adores you but his introductions to new people always need to be slow as this sensitive boy can be easily overwhelmed.

Flash works well within a routine, he has an abundance of energy and a super inquisitive nature which can sometimes lead to him becoming quite lively, he will often revert to ‘mouthing’ and jumping up when he is uncomfortable or unsure.

Flash has a super inquisitive nature and loves to observe what’s going on at a distance. This boy can also be an absolute cuddle monster and adores a snuggle with his favourite people, and will fall asleep next to us when we have the opportunity to sit quietly with him. One of flash’s unique traits is his love of a pamper session! I have never known a dog who enjoys a bath and hairdryer the way he does and he becomes quite docile under the hair dryer whilst having a gentle brush.

Flash’s ideal home would be a quiet an experienced dog owning home (adults only) with humans that have the patience and time to help grow his confidence and who also understand the need to grow calmness in him. Flash has had a few dog friends at the rescue but his high spirted nature can be a bit much for some dogs and he does not seem to like male dogs, for this reason a home where he is the only pooch would suit him best.

Flash walks well on lead but can become very excited when he sees other dogs, walks in quiet areas would be perfect for him, he loves to be outdoors and often just enjoys sitting in the yard with me watching birds, but he will equally enjoy time spent just hanging out with his humans at home. Flash really is a wonderfully, lovable, giant puppy, looking for kind and understanding humans to provide him with the security and love he deserves.

Flash has had a brilliant few weeks. He celebrated his second Birthday and was treated with his first snow day, which he loved frolicking about in. Unfortunately, he did have to spend his birthday in kennels, but I made sure it was still a very special day for him. We hopped in the car, and I took him for a little walk before heading to the pet shop to pick out some birthday treats. He chose a dinosaur toy and a knuckle bone, which he thoroughly enjoyed. I also bought him some special birthday biscuits to keep him going through the week.

After that, I truly spoiled him, and we decided to go to Burger King for a burger! Flash was quite confused at first, but once he had a taste, he couldn’t get enough.

Flash truly is a special boy and will need a special home to match. He can be very wary of strangers and doesn’t always show clear signs if he’s uncomfortable. For this reason, he is muzzled when out on walks, which I make sure to do whenever we go out.

Flash will need an adult-only home with no visiting children. He cannot live with cats or any small animals

The stunning Flash had a little pamper today, which he absolutely loved. He was as good as gold whilst in the bath and sat very contentedly on the grooming table looking out the window enjoying the warmth of the blowers. I have never known a dog to enjoy bath time as much as he does, he becomes quite sleepy and cuddley, it’s the cutest thing.

After his wash and blow dry he got to open some Christmas treats out in the yard sent in from the lovely folks out there that support Many Tears, Flash particular enjoyed the food presents.

Flash really is the most wonderful boy once you get to know him, and we see improvement every day in his sometimes lively and skittish nature. This fantastic boy will make the most awesome and loyal of friend with the person or couple that are prepared to put the time and love into him he so deserves.

Today, Flash and I went on a little adventure to the local pet shop, finishing off with a much-needed pupcup! He was an absolute angel in the car—he hopped right in, buckled up, and sat calmly for the whole journey. I watched him in the mirror as he gazed out at the world passing by. When we arrived, we popped his muzzle on as a precaution since he can sometimes be wary of strangers. Flash wandered around the shop, taking in all the sights and smells, until he discovered the pick-and-mix treats—which of course we had to get. After choosing his goodies, he rummaged through the plushies and picked out a squeaky monkey to take home.

As we headed toward the till, another dog suddenly rushed around a corner and startled Flash, causing him to react. I managed to whisk him away with a distraction, but he became very on edge and tucked himself into me for comfort. A lovely lady then came around the opposite corner and, despite having seen his reaction, kindly stopped to say hello. She happened to be a previous Many Tears adopter, and her own pup is doing wonderfully. She chose to ignore Flash at first to give him space, and once he settled, he allowed her to gently stroke his head. After wishing us well, we carried on with our day.

We sat outside Costa in the sunshine, and Flash absolutely loved his pupcup, so much so that he managed to get it all over his nose.

I’m incredibly proud of Flash today. It was his first outing since arriving in kennels, and I could really see how scared he can be underneath it all, and how much he relies on his human for reassurance. Flash needs someone devoted, patient, and willing to put time into training and working through his reactivity toward other dogs. He truly is a special boy.

Another bleak day at the rescue with the rain pouring down non-stop, but it meant I got to spend some more quality time with the dogsI’ve never been one for poodles but Flash really has stolen my heartToday I really did see his loving and caring side as we cuddled away from the downpour. He rolled around, brought me his toys and chews before receiving belly rubs and head scratches until he fell asleep

If you’ve been to the rescue I’m usually walking Flash around the reception area in order for him to build his relationship with humans and other dogs but it was nice to just have some one on one time with him today, once you’ve created a bond with this boy he is yours for life.Flash’s’ training is still continuing and has managed to learn ‘touch’ where he boops his nose to the designated hand and is in the midst of learning ‘place’.

In a home will still need some training in order for him to thrive.

Flash is still a little mouthy when he gets super excited but is doing much better to when he first arrived with us.

It's been almost 4 months since Flash arrived here and I feel he has been very much overlooked. Deep down he’s a big cuddle bug and thrives on attention.

I tried spending most of my time with him today as kennel life is very stressful for him. We visited the big yard multiple times, went for a stroll and even met 2 dogs on a walk and greeted them with such kindness. Might I say he walks beautifully alongside you!

We met some new people in the reception area, which can sometimes make Flash a little uneasy but he did fantastically and even accepted some treats. For this he is muzzle trained as he can be mouthy when he’s a little too excited!

The last task of the day was to be groomed. I never thought I would see this boy sit still for more than a few seconds, but he amazed me and hopped up onto the grooming table ready to be pampered! And he now looks so good! Flash really doesn’t mind being groomed which will be helpful for the future.

I absolutely adore this beautiful boy. Flash is best described as an oversized puppy at heart. He has a playful, goofy nature but sometimes forgets his size, which can make him a little overexcited and mouthy, especially if he’s unsure or feeling frustrated.

Flash can be a sensitive soul who is often scared of his own shadow and needs plenty of reassurance and gentle confidence-building when faced with new experiences (like the umbrella he discovered today!). Because of this, kennel life is very tough for him, and I truly believe he will thrive so much more in a loving home.

Once Flash trusts you, he shows his affectionate side. He adores snuggling in for a cuddle and loves being pampered.

Flash’s ideal home would be an adult-only household where he can be the only dog. He isn’t aggressive with other dogs but can become boisterous and overwhelming. A quiet location with a secure, good-sized garden would be perfect, ideally with adopters who enjoy long walks and hikes.

He walks beautifully on the lead, enjoys all weathers, and has the stamina to go for hours. While he may sometimes react to new situations or get excitable around other dogs, his confidence and manners are improving every day. Flash will need adopters who are home most of the time or able to include him in their daily lives, as he finds being left alone difficult and may struggle with separation anxiety.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle who has come to us from a home as his owners no longer had time for him and couldn't offer him the exercise he requires. Although he has lived in a home before, Flash is a worried boy who finds new experiences and people quite daunting. Because of this, Flash is looking for an experienced, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time, patience, and love to give. He needs adopters who won’t give up on him and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace.Initially, Flash can be wary of new people and unsure of their intentions, but once you’ve gained his trust, he begins to show his affectionate and loyal nature. He forms strong bonds with those he feels safe around and shows a deep need for companionship. He does not cope well with being left alone and has shown signs of separation anxiety, getting very worried and anxious when left on his own. He will need an adopter who is able to be with him all of the time and who will work on this with him, slowly building up any time he is left. We are told he was crate trained in his previous home, which may help with this process.Flash is particularly sensitive to loud or sudden noises, which can cause him to panic. He feels safest in quiet, familiar surroundings and finds walks outside of the rescue grounds very difficult at the moment. When taken beyond his comfort zone, he becomes overwhelmed and spins in circles in an attempt to return to safety. While he can walk on a lead, his adopters will need to help him grow in confidence very gradually and may need to begin with simply enjoying time in the garden or short walks in peaceful areas.Flash would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as he can be grumbly when meeting other dogs. This is something his adopters will need to work on with him with patience and positive reinforcement. Because of this, he must only be allowed off lead in secure areas with no other dogs present. He also cannot live with cats or small animals and we are told he isn't a fan of pigeons or seagulls.Flash will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and where his adopters will help him settle into a consistent routine so he can feel safe and secure. We are told that he is house trained but he may need some reminders of this in his new homeAlthough he is currently worried about going for walks, he is an active breed who will need to be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. We have been told that he has previously done some agility and scent work, so once his confidence grows this is something he may like to explore again in the future. His previous owners also said he enjoyed being groomed and bathed, though we haven’t yet introduced this at the rescue.This beautiful boy has so much potential in the right hands. If you have the time, experience, and understanding to give Flash the security and stability he needs, he will reward you with trust, loyalty, and love. Please don’t overlook him, he’s waiting for that one special person to believe in him.Flash has an entropion in both eyes, which has been repaired by our vets but does have some dermatitis around his eyes.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Holiday
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I have started to learn about walkies and how fun they can be!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her as the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she came back into our care. Holiday has since moved into foster care where she has settled beautifully and has made some wonderful progress.

Holiday is a very sensitive girl who had very little socialisation before coming into our care. When she first returned to us, she found people incredibly worrying and was very hand-shy. Her first instinct was always to run away, and she wasn't comfortable being picked up or handled. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could react by nipping out of fear, so her adopters will need to understand her body language and never push her further than she is comfortable with.

Since moving into foster care, Holiday has come along in leaps and bounds and is growing in confidence every week. She will now happily stay on the sofa while her foster family are in the room and will even accept gentle strokes while she is there. She knows the command 'touch' and will happily touch her foster's hand when asked. She is also very happy to jump up at their legs when she knows treats are coming! She is becoming much more engaged with people and will often look to her foster for reassurance, wagging her tail and enjoying being part of family life.

Holiday can now have a harness put on, although she is still a little unsure about it and will make herself as heavy as possible while it is being fitted! She has also discovered that walks can be great fun and is now enjoying walks through the park with her bestie. She looks back at her foster constantly and wags her tail, which is lovely to see. She even recently visited a dog activity centre with 11 other family dogs and absolutely loved it!

Holiday has also shown that she can travel well with her canine friends. She doesn't like enclosed spaces, so a crate isn't suitable for her, but she travelled beautifully in the van with her friends using double seatbelts. She was a very good girl throughout her trip back to the centre, where she also had a lovely haircut and her vaccinations.

Holiday will still be looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children. She will need adopters who are experienced with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She relies heavily on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and would definitely like a home with more than one kind and confident resident dog to help guide her.
