name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with another dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium-sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution.

Chewwie has been given the Gift of Life by Paula Elliot

Chewwie is an absolute angel. From the day he arrived on my section, he's been nothing but gentle, loving, affectionate, and just a truly special soul.

Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, I honestly haven't seen that side of him. With me, he's all about cuddles and attention. He'll happily bounce over to say hello and is always looking for affection. He's also got a cheeky side that keeps me smiling. If you leave your folder, phone, or radio lying around for even a second, don't be surprised if Chewwie decides it's his now!

He's a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the pool with his kennel friend. Watching him let loose, have fun, and just be a dog is one of my favourite things. He also loves heading down to the big yard where he can have a good sniff, stretch his legs, and enjoy himself.

Chewwie really is such an amazing dog, and I feel so lucky to know him. Looking after him has been an absolute privilege.

Chewwie is a sensitive and nervous boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and still finds new situations quite overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but he remained worried around men and struggled to relax around the adult sons in the household. He will therefore be looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to home life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts that a home has to offer, especially his cosy beds! He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and slowly build up the amount of time he is left as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium size or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has also learnt how to walk on a lead and now enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will need ongoing support and encouragement as he continues to gain confidence.

Once Chewwie gets to know you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate boy who adores a fuss and cuddle. He has a wonderfully cheeky personality and loves to play with other dogs. He is also a bit of a mischievous boy and has been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as we are told he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially loves hard toys, but softer toys and enrichment items will need to be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. In the right home he will start to come out of his shell and truly flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, affectionate and wonderfully cheeky friend who will make them smile every day.

When Chewwie first arrived he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. When he returned to the rescue he was limping on his front leg and holding it up, we took him to a local vets for an x-ray and no abnormalities or injuries were found, so it's possible that it is a soft tissue injury which should start to feel better soon, but this is something his adopters and their vet will need to monitor.

name: Sundance
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have Grade 4 bilateral luxating patella's, and a bilateral ear infection.

27-08-26 Sundance is a very scared lady who has come to us from a breeder and is such a little heartbreaker. It is so evident that she wants to be brave and is such a sweet girl, but her worries are taking over at the moment. She is going to need a home filled with plenty of TLC, patience and understanding as she slowly finds her paws and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place.

Sundance will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on for comfort as she learns about home life. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Lead walking may be far too scary for her initially, so some gentle garden sniffs and exploring in a secure garden will be a great place to start while she builds her confidence.

Sundance can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind, sensible and able to offer her a calm and quiet environment to settle into. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to adjust at her own pace. With plenty of love, patience and reassurance, we are sure Sundance will slowly begin to settle, discover her confidence and let her beautiful personality shine.

Sundance has come to us with a Grade 4 bilateral patella luxation and will need an operation on both legs. Her adopters will need to be aware of this as it may not be covered by insurance. She has also arrived with a bilateral ear infection which she will receive treatment for.

Sundance has been given the Gift of Life by Linda Towers

name: Lucy
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

27-08-26 Lucy is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably nervous around people. She can be quite vocal when approached and doesn’t yet enjoy being handled, she prefers to keep her distance while she works out that people can be trusted. Lucy is a sweet girl underneath her worries and will need plenty of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she begins to build her confidence.

Lucy is very active and playful with her kennel friends, and this is where we get to see a little more of her personality. She would love a home that can offer her an active lifestyle once she has had time to settle and feel comfortable. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she learns about home life and gains confidence.

Lucy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is willing to go at her pace without putting pressure on her. Lucy will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs will be understood and she can have the time and space she needs to blossom. With patience, love and the support of a confident canine friend, we hope Lucy will slowly learn to trust and show us the wonderful girl hiding underneath her worries.

Lucy has been given the gift of life by Linda Towers

name: Layla
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home! Read below for more.

27-08-26 Layla is a cute little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is a very timid and scared girl who relies heavily on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance. She shakes like a leaf when she is approached, but it is lovely to see that she has a much more playful and active side when she is relaxed with her friends. Layla loves to explore and is clearly a curious girl underneath all of her worries, so we hope that in the right home she will slowly learn that the world isn’t such a scary place.

Layla will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence and learns to trust her new family. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. She would love an active home where, once she has settled and feels comfortable, her family can take her on plenty of gentle adventures and help her discover all the wonderful things the world has to offer.

Layla will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand the time and patience these special girls need. She will need plenty of reassurance and the freedom to progress at her own pace without pressure. With a confident canine companion, lots of TLC and a family willing to help her build her confidence, we’re sure Layla will gradually come out of her shell and show just how lovely she really is.

Layla has arrived with both canines snapped at the tip, and will be assessed by our vets.

Layla has been given the Gift of Life by Linda Towers

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

name: Sianon
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

27-08-26 Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Arctic
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a multi dog household and I am fine with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am starting to really enjoy going for walks on a lead and harness!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

Please meet Arctic! She is a very special girl looking for a very special home with patient, experienced adopters who will never give up on her and who will love her for exactly who she is.

Arctic first came to us from a breeder in 2025. When she arrived, she was an extremely frightened and shut-down girl who found people and handling very overwhelming. Since then, life has been a bit of a rollercoaster for this special girl. She was adopted twice but has sadly found herself back in our care both times. Her first adoption sadly wasn't the right match due to her level of fear, as she could nip if pushed beyond her comfort zone. Her second return came after she accidentally escaped through the front door. In the panic of the situation, she bit her adopter when they tried to catch her, and it was decided that returning her to us was the best option.

Arctic is now settling into foster care, where she has already started to show us more of her wonderful personality. She found the first couple of days quite stressful and spent a lot of time pacing while she explored her new surroundings, but she has settled well and is becoming much more relaxed. She is a very curious girl who likes to know what is going on and will happily follow her foster family from room to room to see what they are doing.

She has been mostly clean during the day, although she has had the occasional overnight accident as she adjusts to her new routine. Arctic sleeps quietly overnight in her crate and is always pleased to see her foster carer in the morning, eagerly waiting for her breakfast.

Arctic is still a very anxious girl and remains particularly worried about being touched or handled. However, she is already making gentle progress. She is slowly learning to trust her foster carer, who is able to carefully pick her up and gently groom her, during which she will accept handling and strokes and actually seems to secretly enjoy it. She has even started choosing to sit on the sofa alongside her foster carer and the other dogs, although she is not yet comfortable with being touched whilst relaxing. Everything is very much on Arctic's terms, and she is showing that, with patience, she is capable of building trusting relationships.

She will need a very special, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs. If she feels pushed beyond her comfort zone, she can make the wrong decisions purely out of fear, so her new family will need to be patient, understanding and committed to helping her continue building her confidence over the long term. She may never be a lap dog, but she is a lovely girl who will show her affection in her own quiet ways, and watching her grow in confidence will be incredibly rewarding.

Arctic had never experienced life in a home before her adoption. Although she spent around six months in her most recent home and is now continuing to learn in foster care, she will still need adopters who understand that she may need a refresher with house training and time to adjust to a new routine.

She has learned all about walking on a lead and harness and now LOVES to go out for walks! She doesn't enjoy having her harness put on, but does allow it awkwardly. She loves meeting new dogs on walks but is wary of meeting people.

One thing Arctic has always loved is the company of other dogs. They are her greatest source of comfort and reassurance, and we feel she would thrive in a home with multiple confident resident dogs, as she relies on canine company so much. She has impeccable doggy manners and gets on brilliantly with all of the dogs in her foster home. She is also happily living alongside a cat in foster care and takes no notice of them.

Arctic is looking for a home that will love her for exactly who she is, rather than who they hope she might become. She is already showing that she enjoys the comforts of home, from curling up on a soft bed to relaxing on the sofa with her canine friends. With experienced adopters, patient guidance and confident canine companions by her side, we truly believe Arctic will continue to blossom and enjoy the happy, secure future she so deserves.

When Arctic originally came to us, she had some fur loss, but this has grown back wonderfully. She also had an enlarged mammary gland, but our vets are not concerned about this at present, although it may require monitoring by her adopters and their own vet. She is currently receiving treatment for some small patches of chronic dermatitis on her lower lip.

Arctic has been given the Gift of Life by Laura Woods

Arctic is really starting to make good progress in foster. She is now lead walking and LOVES to go out. She doesn’t like having her harness put on but allows it awkwardly! Arctic loves meeting new dogs on walks, but is wary of people.

She is slowly getting used to being handled, and I’m able to brush and comb her - I think she secretly quite enjoys it. She is becoming less touch sensitive but will still shy away and often flinches, but this is becoming less frequent. I no longer need a blanket to pick her up. Sometimes when I’m fussing her, she forgets she is scared and relaxes, her eyes start to close which is so sweet.

This fluffballs cheeky personality is starting to emerge, and she will dance around and woof at meal times, she doesn’t like eating from a bowl but will eat off of a clean cloth.

Arctic gets on great with all of the dogs and is often found cuddled up with my other foster dog. She fully relies on other dogs to feel safe - the more the merrier in Arctic’s eyes!

In three weeks, she has come such a long way, she is still a work in progress but wow! I’m so proud of her.

Arctic has been in foster care just over a week. She was very stressed for the first couple of days and did a lot of pacing. She thoroughly explored her new environment and has settled down.

From the start she has been curious about anything going on in the house, and follows us to whatever room we are in. She has been mostly clean during the day, but has the odd accident overnight.

Arctic sleeps quietly overnight in her crate. She seems happy to see me in the morning and eagerly awaits her breakfast! She gets on great with all of the other dogs and ignores the cat. She relies on the dogs and has impeccable doggy manners.

At the moment Arctic is very touch avoidant. Slowly I am making headway with this and am able to pick her up in a blanket and then gently comb her. She will allow me to stroke and handle her during this time. I am gaining her trust and she will sit on the sofa with me and the other dogs, but if I touch her she gets off. It’s still early days.

When the current heatwave ends I will work on the harness training started at the rescue. I think given time and patience Arctic will learn that human touch is a good thing, she already enjoys the comforts of a soft bed and a sofa!

Today little Arctic had what may have been her first professional spa day! She was in desperate need of a good scrub and a blast out of all her undercoat.

Arctic has come a long way since I first met her and although she's still quite nervous to be picked up once she's in your arms she settles quite quickly. She blew me away with how well she took to her bath, and especially the dryer as she needed to have her coat blown out and it didn't seem to phase her one bit. Although she may not admit it I think she enjoyed some parts.

After having a good brush and comb, and being an angel as I trimmed her nails, she let me carry her back home for her dinner but before eating she took herself for a waltz as I'm sure she felt much fresher.

Arctic is such a lovely soul behind her fear and with the right love and patience I think she would blossom beautifully into the little madam I know she can be.

Arctic has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. At the moment, she’s very frightened and she will retreat to the back of her kennel and shake like a leaf when approached.Arctic is looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle in and show her that life can be safe and full of love.She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her and her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life and begins to pick up new skills like house training. She will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and will need to practice first around the home and garden as she gains confidence.With time, love, and gentle reassurance, we believe she can blossom into a loving companion. If you have a peaceful home and a heart big enough to help her on her journey, Arctic could be the one who needs you most.Arctic has an enlarged mammary gland which our vets are not concerned about, and she has some fur loss which we hope will begin to improve and grow back after her spay.

name: Juice
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have learned how to walk on a lead and am enjoying going for walks.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted at the time of my spay.

Juice came to us from a breeder and when she first arrived, she was understandably very shy and overwhelmed by everything around her. She wanted to trust people but was nervous about approaching, often hovering nearby and watching with interest before her worries got the better of her. She has since moved into foster and has made some lovely progress and is settling in well. Juice is still cautious, but she now follows her fosterers around the house and will approach for fuss when they offer their hand to her. She particularly loves belly rubs and will completely relax and close her eyes!

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her settle into her new home. Although she does rely on other dogs for comfort, she can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so she will need a calm, relaxed resident dog who will not disturb her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and on one occasion she did nip her fosterer when they stroked her in her bed. Her new family will therefore need to be confident managing this behaviour, recognising her body language and ensuring she is always left undisturbed when she is resting.

Juice had never lived in a home before moving to foster, but she is already settling in wonderfully. Her toilet training is going really well and she has only had 2 accidents in the home so far. She has also learned all about walking on a lead and harness and is now becoming more confident wearing her harness and she is starting to enjoy her walks. She is also beginning to understand that the home is a safe place, happily relaxing and sleeping near her fosterers and enjoying the company of their resident dog.

Juice will be looking for an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand that she is still learning to trust and who will allow her to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She has already come such a long way in a short time, and we hope that with the right family, she will continue to blossom into a happy and loving companion.

She has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Juice has been given the Gift of Life by Holly Kantolinna

Juice has settled in really well. She is still cautious but follows us around the house although backs off if we approach her as she prefers it if you put your hand out to her. She will then approach us, sniff our hand and accept fuss and scratches. She loves having scratches but her favourite are belly rubs and she will close her eyes and completely relax!

She sleeps well over night in her bed on the floor in our bedroom and will wake us up by walking around the room when she needs to go to toilet. Her toilet training is going really well and apart from 2 accidents early on she goes in the garden either asking to go out or when the back door is open taking herself out to go.

She is getting more confident having her harness on for walk and as long as you put it on slowly, she is happy to have it on. She is starting to walk really well on her lead and enjoys her walks and plenty of sniffs! She has met a few dogs on her walks and as long as they are not too energetic and boisterous she seems happy to meet them and have a sniff! She is ok walking along roads but does startle if there are any loud or sudden noises.

She loves being with us in the house and although she doesn't sit right next to us she enjoys being close by and really relaxes and sleeps. She enjoys being with our resident dog but is also happy to follow us outside or sit with us when our dog isn't there. She's also happy travelling in the car with our dog.

She hasn't mastered going up and down stairs yet so at present we are carrying her up and down. She is starting to go up a few small steps on her walks.

She enjoys her food and will sometimes take treats or food from our hands.  She is a lovely girl who has really progressed in the short time that we have had her and is continuing to develop her confidence.

Juice will need an experienced, adult only home with adopters who can understand and manage her nervousness and recognise when she needs space. She can guard her bed from other dogs, particularly when she has just woken up, so any resident dog will need to be calm and relaxed and not likely to bother her while she is sleeping. She can also be startled by people when she is in her bed and, on one occasion, she did nip when she was stroked resting. Her adopters will therefore need to be confident in managing this behaviour, ensuring she is left undisturbed in her bed and giving her the space she needs to feel safe and comfortable.

Juice has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving forever home where she can begin the next chapter of her life.

She is a wonderful little lady who is feeling a little shy and overwhelmed at the moment, but she is trying so hard to be brave. Juice is already showing lovely signs that she wants to trust people. She will quietly hover nearby, watching you with interest and looking as though she would really like to come over for a gentle fuss, but at the last moment her worries get the better of her. We think that with time, patience, love and plenty of reassurance, her confidence will continue to grow and her true personality will begin to shine through.

Juice will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will need patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time and who will let her make progress without putting any pressure on her. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her that life is full of good things.

As Juice has never lived in a home before, everything will be a brand new experience for her. She will need help with housetraining, learning about household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to all the sights and sounds of family life. She is also yet to learn how to walk on a lead and harness, so her adopters will need to introduce this gently and positively as her confidence grows.

Juice is a lovely girl with so much potential. With a patient family by her side and a canine friend to guide her, we are sure she will blossom into a happy and much-loved companion.

name: Sunny
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

27-08-26 Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave and inquisitive. She will happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

Sunny still looks to her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence. We think she will settle quickly in the right home, and with patience and encouragement, we’re sure her lovely personality will really begin to shine.

Sunny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a lead. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home.

Sunny has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton

name: Queenie
description:
I'd like a patient, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed & have had 10 teeth removed.

06-08-26 Queenie is a scared little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very nervous right now and will growl if we approach her. It is clear that Queenie needs time to settle into her new environment, and we will be taking things slowly with her so that we don't overwhelm her. At the moment, she doesn't yet understand that we are here to help her, and her new family will need to earn her trust with patience and kindness.

We believe that Queenie will need another kind and confident dog in the home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system to help guide her and give her reassurance as she adjusts to home life. As Queenie has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life.

Queenie will need an adult-only home so that she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. She will need calm, patient adopters who are happy to let her progress at her own pace and never rush her. She will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeders and can understand her needs.

Queenie is a gentle girl who has had a difficult start in life. With a quiet home, a confident canine companion, and lots of understanding, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe enough to let her true personality shine through.

Queenie has had 10 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Queenie has been given the Gift of Life by Lyn Guthrie

name: Clippa
description:
I’d like an active home home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with others. No cats or small furries please!

I would love a secure garden with 6ft+ fences that I can run and play in!

I walk on a lead but need some training as I'm strong and can pull.

I did have some separation anxiety which my fosterers have worked on.

I have been spayed! Please read below for more information.

Clippa is a wonderful girl who came to us from a breeder in search of a fresh start. From the moment she arrived, she showed us what a loving and affectionate little girl she is. Whilst in our care at the rescue, Clippa quickly became a favourite with staff and volunteers thanks to her happy nature and love of human attention. She adored going out on walks with volunteers, loved exploring the Welsh countryside and was always happiest when she was close to people getting cuddles and fuss. She also got on brilliantly with her kennel friends and enjoyed the company of other dogs.

She has now moved to a foster home where she has continued to blossom and has settled beautifully into home life. On arrival, she immediately made it her mission to explore every single inch of the garden, showing just how adventurous and inquisitive she is! Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing as she is an active little spaniel who loves to investigate everything around her.

We think that Clippa is a bit hard of hearing and doesn't hear human voices easily. This doesn't slow her down, but, for this reason future adopters will need to be aware that she will likely need to be on lead for her walks and be let off only in secure fields to keep her safe.

Clippa is an incredibly affectionate and people orientated dog who absolutely adores human company. Visitors are instantly greeted by Clippa demanding cuddles, belly rubs and attention, and she will happily snuggle into you whenever given the opportunity. Although she enjoys playing with polite dogs and gets on wonderfully with the resident dogs in foster, people will always be her favourite. When first in foster she did experience some separation anxiety, her fosterers have already worked hard on building her confidence and independence, and her future adopters will need to continue this, gradually building up the time she is left.

She has taken to home life brilliantly and despite having never lived in a home before, she has been clean around the house, with no accidents indoors. She settles beautifully overnight and loves curling up somewhere warm and cosy with her foster family. In fact, she gets so comfortable at bedtime that convincing her to go outside for her final toilet trip can sometimes be a challenge!

Clippa absolutely LOVES her walks and thrives on getting out and exploring the world around her. She would love an active home that understands the busy, intelligent and inquisitive nature of spaniels and can provide her with plenty of mental and physical stimulation. She already walks well on lead most of the time, although she can sometimes be strong and excitable when out and about. At the moment, her recall is non-existent in secure fields as she is far too busy exploring to pay attention, so her adopters will need to be committed to continuing her training with this.

She could happily be homed as an only dog as long as her adopters were around most of the time and had plenty of time to spend with her, but she could also be homed with another kind and playful resident dog. She could live with gentle dog savvy teenagers but cannot live with cats or small furries.

Clippa arrived in our care with bilateral conjunctivitis which responded very well to treatment and continues to be monitored. She also had one tooth removed at the time of her spay.

Clippa is such a happy, loving and affectionate little girl who has embraced her new life with enthusiasm. Whether she is out exploring, making new friends, or snuggled up for cuddles, she throws herself wholeheartedly into everything she does. We think she will make an absolutely wonderful companion for a very lucky family.

Clippa has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

Clippa is the friendliest girl that we have ever fostered. All she wants to do is be with you for cuddles. She has been clean in the house from day 1 and sleeps soundly all night in her bed in our bedroom (although she does like to see if you are awake at 5:30am in case you can give her early breakfast!) She also gets super excited for her bedtime snack routine.Despite her age, Clippa still has quite a lot of pep in her step and LOVES going on long walks and exploring the local countryside, woods and beaches that we have local to us. She is also a huge tennis ball fan! Although Clippa isn't particularly strong, she is very 'busy' so will need someone that can handle her to let her 'Spaniel' to her full potential.Clippa gets on really well with our 2 dogs and likes to snuggle with our Labrador but we also think that she could be an only dog for someone that is around most of the time and willing to build up being left gradually.We think that Clippa is a bit hard of hearing and doesn't hear human voices easily. For this reason future adopters will need to be aware that she will likely need to be on lead for her walks and be let off only in secure fields.Clippas perfect adopters would be someone who is home most of the time, loves snuggly dogs and going for long walks. Some experience of gundog breeds would be useful.

Clippa has now moved into foster and is settling in brilliantly! On arrival, she made it her mission to explore every inch of the garden, so she will definitely need a very secure garden with a minimum of 6ft fencing as she is an adventurous and inquisitive girl.

She has settled beautifully into home life and gets on really well with the resident dogs, although her true preference is definitely humans! Every visitor is instantly greeted by Clippa demanding cuddles, belly rubs and attention. She is such a happy, affectionate little girl who absolutely adores people.

Clippa LOVES her walks and exploring the world around her. She would thrive in an active home that understands the busy, inquisitive nature of spaniels and can keep both her mind and body stimulated. She enjoys playing with polite dogs too, but people will always be her favourite.

At the moment, Clippa has zero recall in secure fields and is far too busy exploring to pay any attention to you! She will need lots of training and practice with this before potentially being allowed off lead and her adopters must be prepared to put the work in.

She has met older children calmly and could be homed with kind and gentle, dog savvy teenagers. She has taken everything in her stride. Around the home she is very clean, has never had a single accident indoors, and settles beautifully overnight sleeping upstairs in the bedroom. In fact, she gets so cosy at bedtime that getting her outside for her final toilet trip can be a challenge and her Foster Dad often has to carry her out because she doesn’t want to leave her warm snuggle spot!

Meal times can sometimes be entertaining as Clippa tends to take a bite, wander off to investigate something else, then come back for another bite as there is always something more exciting to check out! Her absolute favourite things in life are walkies, cheese, and snuggling up with Foster Daddy.

Since arriving in foster, Clippa has decided she loves people so much that she finds being away from them difficult, even for 30 seconds. Her fosterers are already working on her separation anxiety with her and gradually increasing the time she is left, but any future adopters will need to continue working with her and making this a priority with patience, consistency and understanding.

Clippa is an absolute angel girl. She is lovely and affectionate and will snuggle right in for cuddles. Clippa also loves going on long walks and meeting new people.

This week Clippa has been enjoying the sunshine at the rescue, and has been out on some super walks with our lovely volunteers and having plenty of sniff time in our play yards.

Clippa would love a home where she will be able to join in on all the family adventures and have plenty of cuddles.

Clippa is an absolutely lovely Springer Spaniel who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a very affectionate girl who loves human company and will happily snuggle right into you for a cuddle.

Clippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and enjoys their company, so would be happy to share her home with another kind resident dog. She is also confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, as long as her adopters were around most of the time. She couldn't be homed with cats or small furries. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

As Clippa has never lived in a home before, she will need support with house training and learning the basics of home life. With her friendly and affectionate nature, she is likely to enjoy this learning process with her new family.

Clippa can already walk on a lead and enjoys getting out and about, though she can be a little strong at times and can pull, so she will benefit from ongoing guidance and gentle training to help her with her lead manners. She would love to find an active home where she can go on lots of walks and adventures!

Clippa arrived with bilateral conjunctivitis which is already looking much better following veterinary care and will continue to be monitored. She has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay.

Clippa is a loving, affectionate girl who clearly enjoys being close to people and other dogs and we think that she will make a wonderful companion!

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, but I have lived with another dog. See more below.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Quiver, Trevor, Clever Trevor, Trev, Piggy, Pig, Squirrel, Egg Nog Dog

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

River is honestly the sweetest girl once she knows and trusts you.

Recently, I’ve been taking River around our reception area and spending some quiet time with her, helping her learn that people she doesn’t know don’t have to be scary.

River is now happily taking treats from numerous members of staff she doesn’t know, something that might seem so small to some, but for River and everyone who knows her it’s a massive achievement!!

Once River lets you into her world and that special bond is built, she will be your best friend for life. She has so much love to give; she just needs someone willing to take the time to earn it!

I really, really hope River’s people find her soon. It’s heart breaking to see such a loving girl waiting in kennels when I know just how much happiness she could bring to someone’s life.

River may need a little time to trust you, but i can promise you, she will be worth every second.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.
